t: one who has relations with any of the forbidden relations. Who had relations with any of those listed among the prohibitions of forbidden relations (Leviticus chapter 18, and listed above in the list of commandments 1-23). They are called arayot from the plural of 'ervah', since in the heading of the list it says: "None of you shall approach any of his close relatives to uncover nakedness..." (ibid. 18:6), and also in the list itself, for most of the women the prohibition is phrased "the nakedness of... you shall not uncover."
karet. Death at the hands of Heaven (see Hilchot Teshuvah 8:1).
as it says, for whoever does etc.. This verse is found at the close of the passage on forbidden relations, and includes the punishment of karet for all of them.
a fixed sin offering. One that always comes from an animal, unlike the 'rising and falling' offering that varies according to a person's financial means (see Hilchot Shegagot 1:4).
and some of the forbidden relations are punishable by court-imposed death. They will be detailed below in halakhot 4-6.
if there were witnesses and a warning. That there were witnesses to the act, and the transgressors heard a warning not to do the act (for the laws of warning see Hilchot Sanhedrin 12:2).
and did not stop their acts. They continued the transgression despite the warning.
even if the transgressor was a Torah scholar etc.. One who knows that the thing is forbidden is also not punished without a warning.
for warning was not given everywhere etc.. The warning is meant to ensure that the transgression is done deliberately, not to inform the law to someone who does not know it.

some of them are punished by stoning etc.. The death penalties are arranged here according to their severity, from the severe to the lenient (for these methods of execution see Hilchot Sanhedrin 15:1-5).
his wife's daughter during his wife's lifetime. And after his wife's death her punishment is karet only. The same applies to all her relatives mentioned here (below 2:7-8; Hilchot Sanhedrin 15:11).
and a death penalty stated in the Torah without specification etc.. If a death penalty is stated in the Torah without detail, it is death by strangulation.
is by burning. For the punishment of a priest's daughter is more severe (for details see below 3:3), but the Torah was not stringent with the punishment of the man who had relations with her.
a betrothed young woman. One betrothed to another man and not yet married to him (for details see below 3:4-5).
and if she was a betrothed young woman, both of them by stoning... and you shall stone them with stones. The man and the woman, for the Torah explicitly made even the man's punishment severe.
and wherever the Torah says 'they shall surely be put to death, their blood is upon them'. Such as the other forbidden relations mentioned above in halakhah 4.
among those liable for a negative commandment. Those forbidden by a 'you shall not' commandment (for a list see Hilchot Ishut 1:7).
he is lashed, and so is she. Both receive lashes, for one who violates a negative commandment involving an act receives lashes (Hilchot Sanhedrin 18:1).
if unwitting they are exempt from anything. For one does not receive lashes for an unwitting act. And a sin offering is brought only for a prohibition punishable by karet (Hilchot Shegagot 1:1).
the secondary relations. Relatives forbidden by rabbinic decree (for a list see Hilchot Ishut 1:6).
lashes for rebellion. Lashes by rabbinic decree.
among those liable for a positive commandment. Women whose prohibition is stated in the text in positive language (for a list see ibid. 1:8).
he does not receive lashes. For there is no punishment of lashes from the Torah for a positive commandment (Hilchot Sanhedrin 19:3).
one under duress is exempt from anything. He has no punishment (see also Hilchot Yesodei HaTorah 5:4, Hilchot Sanhedrin 20:2).
as it says, and to the young woman you shall do nothing. This verse was said about a young woman who was raped.
but the man who has relations has no duress. He is not considered under duress if he was forced to have relations.
for there is no erection except by will. For the organ does not become erect without the will of the man (see also Hilchot Sanhedrin 20:3).
for a person's inclination and nature compel her to consent. Therefore, even though she is willing, she is treated as one under duress.
the head of the corona. The thickened part at the head of the male organ.

me'areh, from the expression 'she has uncovered her fountain'. This verse was said about one who had relations with a menstruating woman, and the verb 'he'erah' is used as a term for intercourse. The term he'arah is used in the Sages' words for the beginning of intercourse, and for most matters in the Torah it has the law of complete intercourse (see for example Hilchot Yibbum vaChalitzah 2:3).
both the one who begins and the one who completes. They have one law.
who withdrew and did not complete. Who stopped the act and did not insert the entire organ.
and likewise one who has relations with her not in the usual manner. For even relations from behind, anally, are treated as relations in the usual manner (for the source of this law see below 3:15).
a sris chamah. Born with a defect in sexual development (for his signs see Hilchot Ishut 2:13-14).
for this is not intercourse. For in the forbidden relations the term 'seed of emission' is used (see Leviticus 18:20), and intercourse without an erection is not fit to emit seed.

he disqualifies her from terumah. For a woman who is a priest's daughter or married to a priest, and had relations with one disqualified to her, may not eat terumah (for more see Hilchot Terumot 6:7, 8:11). And for this matter even intercourse without an erection disqualifies, since the language of emitting seed is not mentioned in this matter (Yad HaMelech, Hilchot Sotah 1:1).
we give both of them lashes for rebellion. For the act is forbidden, although they are not liable for it.
like one acting unwittingly. Who did not intend to have relations at all.
he is liable. To a sin offering as for an unwitting act, because of the bodily pleasure in the act (see also Hilchot Shegagot 2:7).
and likewise among those liable for a negative commandment and the secondary relations. For there is a prohibition in the act, although there is no punishment for an unwitting act (above halakhah 8).
and she was dead. After she died.
and one who has relations with a treifah etc.. Has relations with a forbidden relation who is near death because of a defect or wound and the like.
he slaughtered in her the two signs. The windpipe and the gullet, so that her death is near.
twitching. Moving her limbs.
and she is exempt from anything. For she is not subject to punishment.
a grown woman. A woman who grew two hairs after turning twelve (Hilchot Ishut 2:1).
less than this... whose intercourse is not intercourse. For intercourse with a girl younger than three years is not considered intercourse at all (see for example ibid. 3:11, 11:3).
and he is exempt. He is not subject to punishment until he grows two hairs after turning thirteen (Hilchot Ishut 2:10).
if he was nine years old or younger, both are exempt. For his intercourse is not intercourse.
the male. A male.

as it says, and you shall not lie with a male, whether he was the one having relations or the one receiving them. The verse made no distinction between the participants in the act, so there is a warning for both.
and if he was a minor. Either the active or the passive partner.
and if the male was nine or younger, both are exempt. For he is not fit for intercourse (as above 1:13).
the androgynos. One with both male and female organs (Hilchot Ishut 2:24).

in the manner of his maleness. In the way one has relations with a male, anally, because from the extra wording of the verses on male intercourse, the androgynos was included as well (see Hilchot Terumot 7:16).

and the tumtum. One whose sexual organs are covered, so it is not apparent whether he is male or female (Hilchot Ishut 2:25). [Note: in the Commentary on the Mishnah, Rambam vocalizes this word tumtom.]
and an androgynos may marry a woman. Because he was included regarding intercourse as a male (Maggid Mishneh), but his betrothal is in doubt (Hilchot Ishut 4:11, Hilchot Terumot 7:14).
and likewise a domesticated animal, a wild animal and a bird. They have the same law.
it is stoned because of him. On his account.
we do not stone the animal. For one nine or younger is not fit for intercourse (as above 1:13).
if unwitting, the animal is not stoned because of them. For no serious sin carrying the death penalty was caused through the animal.
the minor is exempt... as we have explained. Above 1:13.
the sleeper is exempt. For he is under duress.
one under duress is exempt, as we have explained. Above 1:9.
and the witnesses need not see etc.. For the testimony to be accepted, there is no need for an exact view of the act of intercourse itself.
and inserted like a paintbrush in a tube. A thin stick entering a receptacle, which is a metaphor for the act of intercourse.
these are put to death on this sight. The testimony can be accepted, and they can be put to death in court on the basis of testimony of such a sight.
for the presumption of this position is that he inserted. For it is known that if they lay in this position, there certainly was insertion.
one who was presumed to be a close relative. One who was known as a relative forbidden under the law of forbidden relations.
we judge him on the basis of the presumption. On the basis of this knowledge, with no need for proofs.
if he was presumed to be his sister etc.. That this was known and accepted.
and how do we have clear proof that this is his father. For there is no possibility of conclusive testimony proving this fact.
a man and a woman who came from overseas. From another place, and were not known beforehand.
if she was presumed in the city for thirty days... we execute for her. On the basis of the presumption, if she had relations with another, by the law of one who has relations with a married woman.
but within the thirty days. When the presumption is not yet established (for another example see Hilchot Malveh veLoveh 24:4).
who was presumed to be a niddah among her neighbors. Her neighbors knew she was a niddah (see also below 4:9).
one who warned his wife and she secluded herself. He warned her not to be alone with a certain man, and she was alone with him before two witnesses (Hilchot Sotah 1:1-2).
who became defiled. Had relations with that man, and through this testimony she is forbidden to her husband (ibid. 1:14-15).
he receives lashes for her as one who marries a zonah. For she is forbidden to a priest (below 17:1, 18:1).
for the main testimony. The testimony of defilement, which forbids her to her husband.

she has already been presumed a zonah. For the warning and the seclusion were done before two witnesses, and in this situation the Torah trusts a single witness regarding defilement (Hilchot Sotah 1:15).
for he is believed and she may marry him. The father is believed to say about his daughter, before she comes of age, that she is betrothed, and also to whom she was betrothed (Hilchot Ishut 9:10-13).
she is not stoned... until there are witnesses there. For a father is not believed regarding punishments (ibid. 2:23), but only regarding prohibitions (and see further below 18:24).
she is not put to death on her own word. For she is not believed in testimony about herself, although regarding a prohibition we take her words into account (see Hilchot Ishut 9:14-31).
she shall be presumed. As above, halakhot 20-21.

except for his brother's wife who left no son. In this case the brother is commanded to perform yibbum with her (Hilchot Yibbum vaChalitzah 1:1), and the prohibition of forbidden relations is lifted from her (ibid. 1:12).
he is liable for two. For there are two transgressions in the matter, and if unwitting he brings two sin offerings (see below 3:12).
a close relative. A forbidden relation of kinship.

he is liable for two... for the two prohibitions come at once. The prohibitions take effect simultaneously, for when she was betrothed to that relative the woman became forbidden as a close relative and as a married woman. If the prohibitions do not take effect at the same time, 'a prohibition does not apply on top of a prohibition', and sometimes he is liable for only one transgression (see below 17:8; and for its application Hilchot Shegagot 4:1).
therefore. Since his father's wife is a forbidden relation in her own right.
he is liable for two. For his father's wife and for his mother, and if she is still married to his father he is also liable for a married woman (Me'iri).
his wife is a forbidden relation to him. His brother's wife.
a secondary relation. A forbidden relation by rabbinic decree.
as we have explained. Hilchot Ishut 1:6.
born in the home or born outside. Meaning: born within marriage or outside of it.
his father's wife's daughter who is his sister. Who was born from his father.
but he is liable for her as his sister. As stated in the previous halakhah; what need is there to forbid his father's wife's daughter who was born from his father, who is also his sister.
to make him liable for her on this account as well. For two prohibitions.
his sister who is the daughter of his father's wife. Who was born to his father from a woman he married.
and had relations with her. The son of this man, through rape or seduction.
through fornication. Not by way of marriage.

since He forbade the daughter's daughter, He was silent about the daughter. Since the daughter's daughter is forbidden as a relative, the prohibition of the daughter is self-evident (see also Hilchot Ma'achalot Assurot 9:2, Hilchot Tumat Met 1:2).
and its prohibition is from the Torah and not from the words of the scribes. Although it was not stated explicitly in the Torah.
the nakedness of a woman and her daughter. Who is also his wife's daughter (for the prohibition of his wife's relatives see below halakhot 7-8).
whether he married or divorced. Whether he married the one he betrothed or divorced her, the prohibition remains.
both of them are burned. The man and the woman.

him and them. Both of them. And because certainly his wife has no punishment (as she is not a forbidden relation), they learned from the word "them" that the punishment applies only during the lifetime of both, and not after one of them died.
until his wife dies. And afterward she is permitted to him, as the Torah explicitly says she is forbidden only "in her lifetime" (Leviticus 18:18).
from these seven women. The six relatives (above halakhah 7) and his wife's sister (above halakhah 9).
his wife is not forbidden to him. Unlike a married woman who committed adultery or who married another by mistake, who are forbidden to their husbands (Hilchot Gerushin 10:4-10, 11:14).
except for his betrothed's sister etc.. For if he betrothed a woman and afterward married her sister, he must divorce even the one he first betrothed (Maggid Mishneh).

as we have explained in Hilchot Gerushin. 10:8-10, where the case was brought of one who mistakenly married the sister of his betrothed, and the law that his betrothed became forbidden to him. It was explained that this is because it might be thought that the first betrothal did not take effect (because of a condition), and he married the second legitimately, and so he is forbidden to the first, who is her sister. But if he had relations with his betrothed's sister through fornication, the betrothed is not forbidden.
as long as the zonah is alive. As long as that woman is alive.
and his heart is bold with her. He is familiar with her and not embarrassed before her.
and he will come to the transgression of having relations with the forbidden relation. For she is now his wife's relative.
was accused regarding a woman. There is suspicion that he committed adultery with her.
that a bad name came out about him with her. That people said he fornicated with her.
shall not dwell with her in an alley. They are forbidden to live on the same street, whose houses' courtyards open onto it (see also below 21:27).
they whisper behind him. They say that he fornicated.
and the Sages struck him etc.. To keep him far from the transgression.
by way of fornication. Without having betrothed either of them.
like one who had relations with two foreign women. Unrelated, who are not relatives, and there is no prohibition of forbidden relations in this.
she is permitted to him and he may marry her. She is not forbidden to him because of his relatives, and he is permitted to marry her.
and there is no marital status here. There is no marital kinship in intercourse without betrothal.
her daughter. The woman's daughter from another man.
as we have explained. Above 2:3.
the wife of his brother's son. For there is no prohibition of close kinship between a nephew and niece.
as it says, and you shall not hide yourself from your own flesh. A person must take great care of his close family, including marrying those permitted to him.
the wife of a minor. For a minor's betrothal and marriage do not take effect (Hilchot Ishut 4:7, 11:7).
even if she was a yevamah with whom a nine-year-old and one day boy had relations. For this intercourse has acquisition significance (Hilchot Yibbum vaChalitzah 1:16).
a deaf-mute and an imbecile. Who lack understanding, and whose betrothals do not take effect by the Torah (Hilchot Ishut 4:9; for the definition of a deaf-mute see ibid. 2:26).
a tumtum and an androgynos. Who may or may not be male, and whose betrothals are in doubt (ibid. 4:11).
a person of sound mind. An ordinary person, who is not a deaf-mute or imbecile.
doubtfully betrothed or doubtfully divorced. In whose betrothal or divorce a doubt arose.
all are exempt. For there is no fully married woman here.
if her father betrothed her. For a father may accept his daughter's betrothal when she is a minor or a young woman, and the betrothal takes effect by the Torah (see Hilchot Ishut 3:11).
and she became forbidden to her husband. Like any married woman who committed adultery (Hilchot Gerushin 11:14).
as we have explained in Hilchot Sotah. Hilchot Sotah 2:4.

a girl who refuses. A minor who was orphaned of her father or left his authority (through marriage); her betrothal takes effect by rabbinic law only, and she can annul it without a divorce by saying before two people that she does not wish to remain with her husband (Hilchot Ishut 4:7, Hilchot Gerushin 11:1).
permitted to her husband. For by Torah law she is not considered married.
even if he was a priest. Although a priest's wife who was raped becomes forbidden to him (below 18:7), this woman is permitted, since she is not his wife by Torah law.

even if her husband was a mamzer or a natin etc.. Who disqualified her from the priesthood (below 18:3; for their definitions see below 12:22-24, 15:1, Hilchot Ishut 1:7), and even so her punishment is burning because she is a priest's daughter.

and likewise an Israelite's daughter who is a priest's wife, by strangulation. For although she eats terumah and sacred foods like priests (see Hilchot Terumot 6:3), the punishment of burning is unique to one who is a priest's daughter specifically.
betrothed. Engaged, betrothed.
she was an adult. Who is no longer a young woman (see Hilchot Ishut 2:1-2).
who entered the chuppah even though she had no relations. For by entering the chuppah she becomes married, even without intercourse (ibid. 10:1-2).
her father handed her over to the husband's agents. And she left her father's authority by this act (see ibid. 22:2).
it is by stoning. For even a minor is included in 'young woman'.
and she is exempt. For she is not subject to punishment.

and a betrothed young woman, a priest's daughter who fornicated, by stoning. For the punishment of stoning is more severe than burning, and the more severe punishment is always imposed (Hilchot Sanhedrin 14:4).
and all of them by strangulation. As for a married woman, because after the first man she is no longer a virgin.
but if they had relations with her not in the usual manner. Anally, and none of them damaged the virginity.
a freed woman. Who was a Canaanite maidservant and was freed.
even though she was freed and converted and is younger than three years. Although she is presumed a virgin (see Hilchot Ishut 11:1-3).
this is by strangulation. For regarding the law of stoning a betrothed young woman it says: "for she has done a vile thing in Israel" (Deuteronomy 22:21), and these are not daughters of Israel.
in one who spreads a bad name. A husband who claimed after the marriage that his wife fornicated while still betrothed (for more see Hilchot Na'arah Betulah chapter 3).

they stone her at the entrance of her father's house. For it says of her: "and they shall bring out the young woman to the entrance of her father's house and stone her" (Deuteronomy 22:21; and see the next halakhah).
as we have explained. Above 1:4.

for in a married woman there are three deaths. Three kinds of execution for the adultery of a married woman: a betrothed young woman about whom a bad name emerged, by stoning (above halakhot 4-8); a priest's daughter, by burning (above 1:3); and all the rest, by strangulation.

if she fornicated in her father's house... she is stoned at the entrance of her father's house. As it says, "and they shall bring out the young woman to the entrance of her father's house and stone her... for she has done a vile thing in Israel, to fornicate in her father's house" (Deuteronomy 22:21).
before he hands her over. Her father, to the husband or his agents (and see above halakhah 4).

the entrance of the gate of that city. As it says regarding a betrothed young woman who fornicated: "you shall bring them both out to the gate of that city and stone them with stones" (Deuteronomy 22:24).
in the place of stoning. A place designated for stoning those condemned to death (see Hilchot Sanhedrin 12:3).
her conception was not in holiness and her birth was in holiness. Her mother converted while pregnant.
she is stoned at the entrance of the city gate. As in halakhah 9 above, and not at the entrance of her father's house, since she has no lineage through him.
at the entrance of the court. For this entrance is also treated as the city gate (see Hilchot Sanhedrin 15:2).
but only as a mitzvah. Ideally, but if it is not possible, it does not prevent carrying out the sentence.
even though the court cannot put to death etc.. And one might have thought that multiplying liabilities has no significance.
under many names. Many prohibitions.
as will be explained in Hilchot Shegagot. 4:1-2.
there is one who has one act of intercourse and receives many lashes for it. Because it involves several prohibitions together.
as will be explained. Below 17:8-10.
the designated maidservant mentioned in the Torah. For the Torah states a special law for one who has relations with her.
who is half maidservant and half free. She belonged to two partners, and one of them freed his share in her.
and betrothed to a Hebrew slave. Who is permitted a maidservant (see Hilchot Avadim 3:3-4). But one who is not a Hebrew slave is forbidden a maidservant (below 12:11).
if she is completely freed... she becomes a married woman. When the other partner frees her, her betrothal to the man who betrothed her is completed.
as we have explained in Hilchot Ishut. 4:16.
differs from all forbidden intercourse. It has unusual laws, which will be explained below.
for she is lashed, as it says, there shall be an inquiry. Only the woman is lashed, which they learned from the word 'shall be', that it speaks of the woman only.
and he is liable for a guilt offering etc.. And this is an unusual law, since everywhere the laws of the man and the woman were made equal (see below 17:5).
whether unwitting or deliberate... he brings a guilt offering. Unlike other forbidden relations, where only the unwitting offender brings an offering (above halakhah 12).

and one who has relations with her many times... brings one guilt offering. Unlike other forbidden relations, where the unwitting offender brings a sin offering for each act of intercourse, if there were lapses of awareness between them (Hilchot Shegagot 5:2).

one who begins... and did not complete his intercourse is exempt. For it says of her: "and a man who lies with a woman, a lying of seed" (Leviticus 19:20), unlike other forbidden relations, where there is liability for beginning (for definitions and laws see above 1:10).
in other acts of intercourse. Of the forbidden relations.
for two lyings. In the usual manner and not in the usual manner.
but we give them lashes for rebellion by their decree. For the matter is close to a prohibition.
and he brings an offering. When he grows up and has understanding (Hilchot Shegagot 9:3).
as we have explained. Above halakhah 15.
the niddah. For how a woman becomes a niddah see below 5:1-5.
like all the other forbidden relations. As stated above 1:10.
even if she was a minor, three years and a day old. For from this age her intercourse is considered intercourse (above 1:13).

for a girl becomes impure as a niddah even on the day of her birth. If she then sees niddah blood, for the impurity does not depend on age (and this law is regarding her impurity, but liability for intercourse with her applies only from age three and a day, as stated).
and a ten-day-old girl becomes impure with zivah. If she saw blood after a week from birth for three days (for how one becomes impure with zivah see below 6:1-7).
from oral tradition. The Sages' tradition.
for there is no difference. There is no distinction, and their law is the same.
all seven days. The seven days from when she saw niddah blood.
even if she saw only the first day. That she saw blood for only one day, and nevertheless is impure and forbidden for seven days.

a woman who gives birth to a male etc.. A woman who gives birth to a male is impure for seven days, and one who gives birth to a female is impure for fourteen days (for the laws of a woman who gave birth see below 10:1).
all the days of her zivah and her counting. For in order to become pure, a zavah counts seven clean days after the flow of blood stopped (below 6:8).
whether a maidservant or a freed woman. Their law is the same (see also Hilchot Metamei Mishkav uMoshav 2:10).
all the days of her impure flow shall be like the days of her niddah. That all the days she is impure as a zavah, her law is like that of a niddah.
she shall be impure like the days of the niddah of her infirmity. Said of one who gave birth to a male, whose impurity equals the days of niddah impurity.
and she shall be impure for two weeks as in her niddah. Said of one who gave birth to a female.
depends on the days. On the fixed count of days, after which she can become pure.
when she has immersed in a mikveh. And thereby became pure from her impurity.
for Scripture made it depend on days and immersion. And one of them alone is not enough.
as it says, and he shall bathe in water. Said regarding the impurity of emission of seed.
a paradigm. A halakhic source, a law that serves as a basis for other laws learned from it.
gentiles are not liable for them etc.. For in the law of impurity it says: "speak to the children of Israel...".
that they will always be like zavim. When they reach the age fit for intercourse (see further Hilchot Metamei Mishkav uMoshav 2:10).
regarding impurity and purity. That they convey severe impurity. For the prohibition of intercourse see below 12:2.
the thirty-three for a male. The days that follow the seven days of impurity of a woman who gave birth to a male.
and the sixty-six for a female. The days that follow the fourteen days of impurity of a woman who gave birth to a female.

and it does not prevent the woman from her husband. This blood does not make her impure and does not forbid her to her husband (and this is by the basic law; for the stringency of the Geonim see below 11:6-7).
even though the blood is flowing. Dripping, because it is not impure at all.
their immersion is by day. The time of their immersion is on the last day of their counting, and they need not wait until evening.

all seven are as a niddah and she immerses on the night of the eighth. Those days in their entirety are days of impurity, and the time of her purification is only after they pass, namely the night of the eighth.
for a woman who gave birth is like a niddah. For Scripture equated them with each other.
as we have explained. Above 4:2.
she was delayed many days. Past the time she should have immersed.
she may immerse only at night. Even though seven full days have already passed for her.
they will err and another niddah will come to immerse on the seventh. For they might think a niddah is allowed to immerse by day even if the seven days have not yet passed.
she was ill. So that immersing at night is difficult for her.
the bandits. The robbers.
the cold. The chill.

she immerses on the eighth day... by day. For the requirement to immerse at night even after the seventh day is not by strict law but a rabbinic enactment out of concern for error, and when there is hardship it can be relaxed.
a set cycle. A fixed cycle for the appearance of niddah blood (below 8:1-2).
in a presumption of purity for their husbands. The assumption is that they are pure (see also Hilchot Metamei Mishkav uMoshav 4:7).
that she be presumed a niddah among her neighbors. Her neighbors know that she is a niddah (see also above 1:22).
he need not ask her. Because when he left she was pure, and she is still in her presumption.
it is permitted to have relations with her outside the time of her cycle. For only at the time close to seeing blood is it forbidden to have relations with her (to be explained below halakhot 12-13).
and if he left her a niddah. At the time he left, she is presumed impure until she says she became pure.
and I told you at first in jest and mockery. What I said, that I am impure, was in jest.
and if she gave an excuse for her words. An explanation and reason why she first said she was impure and retracted.
her husband demanded her. For relations.
I became impure. That she felt blood come out of her (see also Hilchot Shegagot 5:7).
in his erection. While the organ is erect.
for his pleasure in withdrawal is like in entry. For there is pleasure even in withdrawing while erect.
and the same applies to other forbidden relations. That if he learned that she is forbidden to him, he must not withdraw immediately (Hilchot Shegagot 5:7).
and he remains and does not move. Remains without motion.
until the organ dies. In which state there is no liability for intercourse (see above 1:11).
near her cycle. Close to the time when she usually sees blood.
and you shall separate the children of Israel from their impurity. You shall command them to withdraw and keep away from impurity.
it is forbidden to have relations from the beginning of the day. Which is the time near her cycle, as will be explained in the next halakhah.
the time of the cycle. That day or night on which she is expected to see blood.
at six hours of the day. After six hours from the start of the day.
from the beginning of the day. From the time of sunrise.
she is forbidden to have relations until evening. For the entire day is the time of the cycle.
to examine themselves after relations. Lest she became impure during the relations.
with a cloth prepared for him. A piece of cloth prepared for him.
since she is believed about hers. To say whether she examined immediately and saw blood, and both became impure.
she is believed about his. To say that blood was found there, and to distinguish whether it is from him or from her (and see Hilchot Shegagot 5:6).
worn. Worn, not new but old and soft, on which examination is easy.
witnesses. Those who testify to the presence of blood.
the modest ones. Women who add stringency in their purity (see Hilchot Metamei Mishkav uMoshav 4:7).
and a woman who has no cycle. Who has no fixed cycle of seeing blood.
she is forbidden to have relations until she examines. And ensures that she is pure, because at any time she might become impure without knowing (see also Hilchot Ishut 25:7).
and one after relations. Like all women (above halakhah 14).
but a woman who has a cycle does not need a cloth before relations except for modesty. And not by law, for she is in a presumption of purity (as above halakhah 9).
even a pregnant woman and a nursing woman etc.. Although they are presumed not to see blood (below 9:4-5), they must examine lest they became impure.
a virgin. Who had relations for the first time, as long as the blood coming from her is considered virginity blood, which does not defile (for more see below 5:18).
and sits on blood of purity. A woman who gave birth, after the days of her impurity (see above 4:5).
for the blood is flowing from her. That they are pure even though they see blood.
they need not examine their two cloths for each act of intercourse. For we rely on the presumption of purity for this (above halakhah 9).
wipes... after each act of intercourse all night. Lest on one of the occasions she became impure, and the blood would not remain until after the last time.
until she examines first with another cloth. Lest she became impure in that act of intercourse.
drawn out. Smeared.
for its presumption is from the wiping. For this is the form of blood that comes from the act of wiping.
round. A drop that was not smeared.
a louse that was killed under the pillow. A louse that was crushed on the cloth while it was kept under the pillow.
the one examined for her. That is clean of blood.
and she smeared it on her thigh. She pressed it onto her thigh.
and we do not say perhaps when she smeared it on her thigh a louse was killed. For that is not plausible in this case.

like a gris and more. The measure of a gris is like a split fava bean (a kind of legume), and in such an amount it is certain that the blood is not from a louse (its nature and measure will be explained below 9:6).
she is permitted to have relations when she becomes pure a second time. For it was not proven that there is a connection between the relations and the impurity.
she is forbidden to have relations with this husband forever. For she is presumed to become impure at the time of relations (see also Hilchot Ishut 25:8).
something on which to rely. Another cause, to which it can be said that the seeing of blood was due.
a wound. A sore.
different. Unusual.
inside the source. In the womb.
and even though blood comes out of the source. This is not niddah blood.
she must be divorced. For she is unfit for her husband for relations (Hilchot Ishut 25:8), as she is presumed to see blood during relations.
and she is permitted to marry a second. For with regard to him she is not presumed to see blood during relations.
and she is forbidden to marry until she recovers from this illness. For she is presumed to see blood during relations with anyone.
how does she examine herself etc.. Whether the blood she sees during relations comes from the source or from the sides.
a lead tube with its mouth turned inward. A tube of lead whose rim is bent inward, to prevent injury during the examination.
a paintbrush with a ball of wool on its end. A thin stick with a lump of wool at its tip.
to the neck of the womb. To the opening of the womb.
it is known that the blood she sees is from the pressure of the sides. From the pressure applied to the sides during relations blood comes out, and it is not impure.
as we have explained in Hilchot Ishut. 25:8.

becomes impure through duress. Even if the seeing of blood was caused by some act, and did not come from the body's natural cycle (unlike a zav, who does not become impure if he saw by duress, Hilchot Mechusrei Kapparah 2:1-5).
are engaged with each other. Are having relations.
since she saw blood from anywhere. In any case.
like a mustard seed. The size of a mustard seed, an example of a very tiny size.
in the outer chamber. Outside the womb.
and even though the blood did not go outside. It is still inside the body.
dripped. Flowed.
since it came out from between the teeth. That it is outside the neck of the womb.
at the time of completing intercourse. Inserting the entire organ (above 1:10).
and the teeth themselves are like inside. Blood found there is treated as if it were inside, and does not defile.
the Sages gave a parable about a woman. In describing the structure of a woman's body.
innermost. Deep in the body.
the long place whose top gathers together at the time of pregnancy. The opening of the womb, which closes during pregnancy.
the vestibule. A vestibule.
an entrance room to the womb. An entrance chamber.
the organ enters the vestibule. For even the outer house is included in the term vestibule.
according to the fingers. A euphemism, meaning according to the size of the organ.
the two eggs of a woman. The ovaries, in which the reproductive cells are found.
and the paths in which her seed ripens. The fallopian tubes, in which the ova reach the capacity to be fertilized.
a lul. A term for a vertical passage between parts of the house.
enters inside the lul. Beyond the place of that opening.
from the chamber. From the womb, the source (above halakhah 3).
except for blood of purity. Of a woman who gave birth (above 4:5).
and blood of hardship. Which comes from labor pains.
as will be explained. Below 7:1.
in the kidney. A kidney.
from the lul and inward. Toward the inside of the body.

and one is liable for it for entering the Temple. One impure with niddah impurity who entered the Temple is liable to karet if deliberate and an offering if unwitting (Hilchot Biat HaMikdash 3:12-13).
and we burn terumah and sacred offerings because of it. If the impure person touched terumah foods or offerings, they must be burned (Hilchot Terumot 12:2, Hilchot Pesulei HaMukdashim 19:1).
and we do not say perhaps it came down from the upper chamber. We do not worry that this is blood that came from the upper chamber, which is pure.
those found here. From the lul and inward.
in the vestibule outside the opening. Toward the outside.
we do not burn etc.. By the law of doubtful impurity.
a liquid. A fluid.
green. Yellow.
whose thickness is like blood. Whose viscosity is like that of blood.
and whose appearance is not the appearance of blood. In terms of its color.
how is its color. What is the shade in question.
like the stream that first comes out of bloodletting. The first flow of blood that comes out during bloodletting.
and he brings it near. He brings the doubtful color close to it, and compares the colors (below halakhah 11).
like the ray of saffron. The shining (radiant) part of the saffron.
with the clump of earth on it. While it is still attached to the clump of earth, so that it remains moist.
from its clearest part. The shiny part.

its middle stalk. Which is the brightest part of the saffron. (The identification of the stalk and leaves mentioned here is unclear, but perhaps it refers to the stigmas of the saffron, which are reddish-yellow in color.)
from the valley of Sikhni. The Sakhnin valley in the Galilee.
like a garlic peel. Some thickness.
and he muddies them. Mixes the water and earth until the water is muddy.
and he estimates by them at its time and place. He compares them to the blood immediately, at the same time.
and if they settled. The earth sank and the water became clear.
deep. Dark.
faded. Light.
diluted. Mixed and faded.
like mixed wine. Wine mixed with water.
Sharon wine. Wine from grapes of the Sharon region.
undiluted. That it not have been previously mixed with water.
and new. That it not be old wine (for the definition of old wine see Hilchot Mekhirah 17:6).
and a woman is believed etc.. The sage need not compare the colors; it suffices that he know which color is meant.
and he evaluates. Assesses.
in the glass of a cup. Through the transparent wall.
its weight is a maneh and it holds two logs. So that the cup's wall is relatively thin compared to its capacity.
and it shall not be dark. If the cup is too small or its walls too thick.
and he makes a shade with his hand. Shields the blood with his hand.
its appearance. Its shade.
for all these matters. The examinations by comparison.
visual recognition. Immediate recognition based on past experience.
a woman who miscarries a piece. A pregnant woman who miscarried a piece of flesh without defined form.
and if not, pure. For the piece is not considered blood.
gathered. Collected.
impure. Because the piece is torn and the blood touched her womb (see below halakhah 16), and it is not blood of a piece.
yavchushin. A kind of gnat.
dissolved. Dissolved in water.
for it is blood that congealed. This is blood that coagulated.
and anyone who sees dry blood is impure. For niddah blood defiles whether moist or dry (Hilchot Metamei Mishkav uMoshav 2:1).
a day and a night. A full twenty-four hours.
these are from a wound. As a result of a sore.
a tube. A thin pipe.
whether she is standing... or sitting. While standing or sitting.
even if her body felt it and shook. Similar to what she felt at the time of seeing blood.
for urine does not come from the chamber. It does not flow from the womb, but from another place.
in the hollow or the kidney. In the internal organs.
blood of a wound. Blood of an injury, since it came following the tearing of the hymen.
a minor. Younger than twelve (Hilchot Ishut 2:1).
never saw blood in her life. Her monthly cycle has not yet appeared.
until the wound heals. Until the sore is healed.
for any blood she sees is from the wound. And we do not worry about niddah blood since her time to see has not come.
a young woman. Who grew two hairs after turning twelve and a day (Hilchot Ishut 2:1).
and withdraws. Separates from her after the relations.
as if it were the beginning of a niddah. That she is impure for seven days (below 6:2).
and an adult. When six months have passed since she became a young woman (Hilchot Ishut 2:2).
we give her the whole first night. That she is not impure for all of it, even if she sees blood.
intermittently. With interruptions, and not necessarily consecutively.
even if it did not heal for a year. Even if the sore did not heal for a whole year.
and became a young woman under her husband. That while married she showed signs of maturity.
she saw the blood when she would stand etc.. For certain bodily conditions cause the wound to open and bleed.
this is niddah blood. And the blood cannot be attributed to the hymen, for if so it would have come after the relations.

one who has relations with a girl younger than three. Although in most halakhic matters intercourse at this age is not considered intercourse (see above 1:13) and she is considered a virgin, nevertheless we assume that the bleeding stems from the tearing of the hymen and is not niddah blood.
and blood of hardship. Blood that comes during labor pains (see below 7:1).
it is all one blood and one source. All these bloods are of the same type, and from the same source.
and only by times does its law change. For impurity is determined according to the time of seeing, although in reality there is no difference between those bloods.
when a woman first sees blood. For the first time in her life.
the time that she fixed for her niddah. The beginning of the period of time in which she becomes a niddah when she sees blood (to be explained further below halakhah 4).
she is a niddah all seven days. During those seven days.
whether she saw only the first drop. Even if she saw one drop on the first day, she is impure for seven days.
outside the time of her niddah. Outside the time in which she becomes a niddah.
and it is a law given to Moses at Sinai etc.. For so is the law transmitted by tradition.
only eleven days. For if she sees blood on those days her law is that of a zavah.
that a cycle was fixed for her at their beginning. And they were fixed as the time in which, if she sees blood, she will be considered a niddah (as above halakhah 2).
whether she saw blood in them or did not see. Even if she did not see blood and did not become impure, these days are called 'days of niddah'.
and take care with these two names. Remember these two terms, whose importance is great for the laws of niddah and zavah, as will be explained further.
from the day a cycle is fixed for her. From the time she first saw, and a time was fixed for her for the days of niddah.
that the cycle be uprooted to another day. That if she gave birth, the counting of days begins anew, as below.
seven and after them eleven. In a continuous cycle.
and she must be careful with the count. The woman must be careful in counting the days.
as will be explained. Below 7:12.
and the minimum of 'days' is two, the 'many' is three. The word 'days' in the plural refers to at least two, and the word 'many' adds one more day.
a minor zavah... a major zavah. The difference in their laws will be explained in the next halakhah.
one who watches day for day. The manner of watching will be explained below halakhah 9.
counting seven. Counting seven clean days, without seeing any blood.
and bringing an offering. For a zavah brings bird offerings for atonement (below halakhah 11, Hilchot Mechusrei Kapparah 1:3).

regarding impurity and the prohibition of intercourse they are equal. For there is no difference between the zavot in the degree of their impurity (Hilchot Metamei Mishkav uMoshav 1:2), and likewise in the prohibition to have relations with them.
that entire day is impure. For until evening she is impure, even if she has not seen more blood.
and she watches. Waits.
she rises early the next day and immerses after the sun has risen. She immerses the next morning, after the night of watching has been completed (and see Hilchot Metamei Mishkav uMoshav 5:6).
whether on its night after she immersed. On the night between the first day and the second day, after she immersed from the impurity of the first day.
seven pure days without blood. And these are called 'seven clean days' (above halakhah 8).
and on the eighth day she brings her offering. And she is not pure to eat sacred food until she brings her offering (Hilchot Mechusrei Kapparah 1:1).
as if she had not immersed. For the time of her immersion has not yet come, and she immerses again the next day.
and she is like a niddah who immersed within the seven. For the days of her impurity were not completed, and even if she immersed she does not become pure (above 4:6).
exempt from karet. And he is not treated like one who had relations with a zavah (explained above 4:2), if she indeed did not see blood until evening.

and this woman is bad conduct, for her intercourse and touch are in suspense. Having relations with this woman is improper conduct, for her status is uncertain until it is clarified at the end of the day of watching whether she saw or not (see also Hilchot Metamei Mishkav uMoshav 5:6).
the day was completed after the immersion and she did not see blood. As explained above, halakhot 9-11.
and if she saw blood on this day after she immersed, she turns out to be a zavah retroactively. It became clear that she was a zavah the whole of that past day.
are liable for an offering. By the law of one who had relations with a zavah unwittingly, who is liable for a sin offering.
a zavah who counted. A major zavah (above halakhah 11).
she nullified everything. The whole count is void.
from after the impure day. From the day after it, for the clean days must be consecutive without blood.
she discharged seed. That she had relations, and the seed came out of her body.
she nullifies one day. That day is not counted in the seven, but it does not cancel the seven clean days.

because she is like a zav who saw an emission, who nullifies one day. For a zav must count seven clean days from the day he stopped seeing flow, and if he emitted seed during them, that day is not counted for him (Hilchot Mechusrei Kapparah 3:1-2).
she is not a major zavah but went out of minor zivah into niddah. For the third day belongs to the days of her niddah, and therefore it does not combine with the first two to make her a major zavah.
for on the twelfth day her niddah begins. For the days of zivah are only eleven days (above halakhah 2).
as we have explained. Above 5:5.

and what is this that is written in the Torah, or if a woman has a flow beyond her niddah. From what the verse says, it is understood that zivah can be adjacent to the days of niddah. However, above it was explained that if she saw adjacent to the days of niddah before them, she is not a zavah.
on the eighth of her niddah. That is, adjacent to the seven days of niddah after them, and not before them.
first, second and third of the eleven days. That immediately follow the days of niddah.
she saw blood on the eleventh of the days of her zivah. Which is the last of the days of zivah.
and immersed in the evening, which is the night of the twelfth, and had relations. And did not watch a pure day against the impure day.
for she is impure and the one who has relations with her is impure. For in this matter the immersion did not help (see also Hilchot Metamei Mishkav uMoshav 5:7).
and they make a lying and sitting impure. They defile what they sat or lay on.
for the twelfth day does not combine. For it belongs to the days of niddah.

the immersion of this night helped her to save her from the offering. Which depends on liability for karet. And since the next day does not combine for zivah, the immersion helps and is not considered immersion before the time (compare above halakhah 12).
like the law of any minor zavah. Who watches a pure day against the impure day (above 5:9).
exempt from anything. They have no punishment at all, and they also do not make a lying and sitting impure.
there is nothing in it. The seeing does not make her impure as a zavah retroactively (compare above halakhah 14; and see also Hilchot Metamei Mishkav uMoshav 5:8).
at twilight. Which is doubtfully day and doubtfully night.
on the ninth and the tenth. Of the days of niddah, which are the second and third days of the days of zivah.

she is a doubtful zavah. For it is uncertain whether the seeing was at the beginning of the eighth night, which is the first of the days of zivah, or at the end of the seventh day, which is of the days of niddah and does not combine for zivah.

and she saw at the end of the eleventh day at twilight. For it is uncertain whether she saw on the eleventh day and is a zavah, or saw on the night of the twelfth and this is the beginning of niddah, and this seeing does not combine for zivah.
within the days of her niddah. Before the end of the seven days of niddah.
and did not examine until many days after her niddah. At the time suitable for zivah blood.

we do not say perhaps all those days she was impure. We do not worry that she saw blood again during her niddah days, and the seeing continued until many days later, and she must worry that she may be a zavah.
in a presumption of purity. In the presumption that she did not see blood.
she examined herself and found impure. During the days of niddah.
and at twilight. When the days of niddah impurity end.
she did not examine herself in order to separate from niddah impurity. To ensure that she sees no more blood.
she is a doubtful zavah. For it was presumed that the blood did not stop on the seventh day, and perhaps it continued three days.
and if she found impure she is a certain zavah etc.. For at first she was presumed to be seeing, and this presumption was not canceled, since at the end it was also found so.
and the first day of niddah... the source was presumed open. And the examination of the first day does not create a presumption of purity.
on the first of the days of counting. Of the seven clean days.
she is in a presumption of purity. For at first she was presumed pure, and this presumption was not canceled, since at the end it was also found so.
and on the eighth day. Which is after the seven clean days.
she is in a presumption of purity. For all seven clean days were presumed pure, since she was found pure at their beginning and after them.
she examined on the third day of her zivah and found that the blood had stopped. And she begins counting seven clean days the next day (above halakhah 9).
she is in a presumption of purity. For here too all seven clean days were presumed pure, since she was found pure before them and at their end.
and the same applies to a zav in all these examinations. For the presumption of purity helps in counting seven clean days for his purification (see also Hilchot Mechusrei Kapparah 3:3).
she must sit seven clean days out of doubt. To be stringent, in case her law is that of a zavah.
and she immerses on the eighth night. Like a niddah, who immerses specifically at night (above 4:6-8).
and brings the offering of a zavah and it is not eaten. For the bird sin offering that comes for a doubt is not eaten but burned (Hilchot Pesulei HaMukdashim 7:10).
as will be explained in its place. Hilchot Mechusrei Kapparah 1:6.
that she began to suffer and labor pains seized her. That the pains of contractions began for her.
this is called blood of hardship. Because it came out while she was in difficulty giving birth.
in the days of her niddah... in the days of her zivah. Explained above 6:6.
from oral tradition. An oral halakhic tradition.

her flow is from herself and not from the child. For in zivah the blood flows by itself and not because of something else, and if it comes because of the child, this blood does not have the law of zivah.
there is no hardship for miscarriages. The special law of blood of hardship does not apply to the birth of a stillborn, and it is treated as zivah blood.
dripping and coming down with the pains and distress for fourteen days. For the blood flows for a very long time, together with labor pains.
and she is giving birth with a flow. For there is no purity of blood of hardship here (and its law will be explained below halakhah 5).
when does this apply. That blood of hardship is pure.
but she grows more and more in hardship. The pains continue.
and she got relief from the pains. She had rest from the contractions.
even though the blood did not stop etc.. For the purity of blood of hardship does not depend on the blood, but on its being due to the pain of birth.
hardship close to the birth, she is not giving birth with a flow. For the closeness of the hardship to the birth proves that the blood came because of the child.
ease. A time without distress.
the third of her seeing fell on the day of birth. That she saw for two days before it.
for the day of birth is adjacent to the hardship. On the day before it.

and it is not known what she miscarried etc.. Whether this was a stillbirth through which she became impure as a woman who gave birth, or not (see below 10:1-11). Likewise it is not known whether she saw blood at the time of the miscarriage, so that she would be a major zavah by seeing blood for three consecutive days (see below 10:17, Orah veSimchah).
she must sit seven clean days. By the law of a zavah (above 6:8).

and afterward she will have blood of purity. For if she sees blood afterward, until the fortieth day from the birth of a male or until the eightieth from the birth of a female, it will be pure (above 4:5).
if she gave birth to a male. For whom the impurity of birth is seven days (above 4:2).
she counts seven clean days. By the law of a zavah, and afterward immerses for the impurity of birth and of zivah.

and if she gave birth to a female. For whom the impurity of birth is fourteen days (above 4:2), and it is possible that she counts seven clean days for her zivah, but she is still impure because of the birth.
she is forbidden to her husband until the night of the fifteenth. When the days of birth impurity for a female end.
if she saw blood three. After the birth of a female.
for all fourteen she is like a niddah. Even if she sees no blood in them.
they count for her toward the counting of seven. Clean days, even though she is impure in them from the side of the days of niddah or birth.
as will be explained. Below halakhot 10-11.
that her blood did not stop. That she did not have seven clean days of blood after she gave birth.
she has no blood of purity. For as long as she has not become pure from her flow, she is forbidden to her husband.
she immerses and is permitted to her husband immediately. Through this she becomes pure from the impurity of zivah she had.
for all the days of purity are not suitable either for niddah or for zivah. Therefore this blood does not make her impure.

but the blood itself is impure and defiles. The blood that flows from her as long as she has not immersed defiles by touch and carrying (Hilchot Metamei Mishkav uMoshav 1:8), as long as she has not immersed.
within eighty. Within the days of purity blood of the previous birth.
until she miscarries the child. And if she miscarried, she counts days of impurity and purity anew, from the time of the miscarriage.
impurity of a male. Seven days.
impurity of a female. Fourteen days.
and the days of completion. The days of blood of purity, until the completion of forty days for the birth of a male and eighty for a female.
within the clean days. In the middle of the seven clean days of a zavah.
it does not cancel. She does not need to count seven clean days anew.
and the days of hardship count for her toward the seven. And she need not count clean days in their place.
and the days of birth count for her toward the seven. If she did not see blood in them (above halakhah 6).
even though she is impure in them. Because of the birth.
once she became pure from her flow. That she stopped seeing zivah blood.

or niddah impurity. For it is possible that her days of niddah will come within the seven clean days (see above 6:6), and if she saw blood in them and became impure, the impurity does not cancel the count.
these count for her etc.. They are counted, as stated in the previous halakhah.
but she makes up for the days she counted. For those days in which she saw are not counted, and she must add days to match them.
for only a seeing of zivah cancels everything. For only a seeing during the days of zivah cancels the count (above 6:15).
but these cancel only their day. They cause only that day not to be counted.
once you understand all the principles we have explained. On the basis of understanding the principles mentioned in these halakhot.
that it is possible that she will see... and not be a zavah. That she will not be considered a major zavah, because there is no combining of three consecutive days of zivah.
two before her niddah. The last two days of the days of zivah.
and two after the days of niddah. The first two days of the days of zivah.
after the days of completion. After the completion of the days of purity of the birth.
it is the beginning of her niddah. From this time one starts counting the cycles of the days of niddah and zivah (explained above 6:2-6).
and we pay no attention to cycles from before. We do not take into account the cyclical count that existed before the birth.
at twilight, she is a doubtful niddah. For it is uncertain whether it is from the day, which is of the days of purity, or from the night, which is of the days of her niddah.
we have already explained that the niddah etc.. Above 4:6.
and a minor zavah watches one day. Above 6:9-10.
and a major zavah counts seven clean days. Above 6:11.
only eleven days. Above 6:3.

this that the Sages said will be clear to you. It will be possible to understand the calculations the Sages made regarding niddah, for a woman who sees blood for a fixed number of days and afterward stops seeing for an equal time, as will be detailed below.
at first she has relations on the eighth night. On which she became pure from her days of niddah.
and on the eighth day. The following day, and she did not see blood on it.
and has relations on each of the eighteen days. On the other days remaining from the cycle of the days of niddah and zivah.

only four nights. For she sees one day and watches the next day, and at night she is permitted, and so on. So it turns out that she has relations on the night of the eleventh, the night of the thirteenth, the night of the fifteenth and the night of the seventeenth, and sees the next day after them.
if she saw the blood every day from the beginning of the night. And not by day, she is forbidden on those nights that were mentioned.
she has relations only on the eighth etc.. For she does not need to watch on it.
has relations on the eighth. On which she became pure from her days of niddah.
and on the twelfth. For the ninth and tenth are days of seeing, and the eleventh is a day of watching.
and the sixteenth. For the thirteenth and fourteenth are days of seeing, and the fifteenth is a day of watching.
and the twentieth day. For the seventeenth and eighteenth are days of seeing, and the nineteenth is a day of watching.

for one of them is watching for the two impure ones adjacent to her niddah. For she saw after her niddah on the eighth and ninth days, and must watch one day against them, and two pure days remain for her.
has relations on one day after her niddah. For on the eighth day she is pure, but she sees the next day, and never has seven clean days.
the three adjacent to her niddah. That she will not see until the eleventh day of her niddah.
in the five days adjacent to her niddah first. That she will not see until the thirteenth day of her niddah.
an impure week in which a zavah is established. In which there are three consecutive days of seeing.
and it turns out she has relations only one week. In the second week immediately after the days of her niddah.

and likewise all her days she has relations eighteen days etc.. For her days of purity depend on the cycle of days of niddah and zivah, seven days of niddah and eleven days of zivah. And sometimes the days of impurity will fall on three consecutive days of zivah (or more), and she will become a zavah, and will have to count seven clean days during the seven days of purity, and will not be able to have relations in them. And if three of the days of impurity do not fall within the days of zivah, she does not become a zavah, and in the seven pure days she can have relations at least in part. According to the calculation that will be explained in the following halakhot, it turns out that she has relations eighteen days in every eighteen weeks. And at their end a cycle is completed in which she returns to seeing at the beginning of the days of her niddah.

the fifth week she is a zavah. For in the second week the eleven days of zivah began. And of the third week in which she saw, four days were days of zivah and three days of niddah. She became a zavah and counted in the fourth week seven clean days, of which four were days of niddah and three days of zivah, so that the whole fifth week falls in the days of zivah.
the sixth week in which she is pure for counting. In it there is one day of zivah and six days of niddah.
the seventh week a zavah. In it there is one day of niddah and six days of zivah, and she becomes a zavah.
the eighth week for counting. Five of its days are days of zivah and two are days of niddah.

the ninth week... five days of it of the days of niddah and two from the beginning of the days of zivah. And she did not become a major zavah, since she did not see on three days of zivah, and she needs no seven clean days, only one day of watching.
the tenth pure week. In which there are seven days of zivah.

the eleventh week... two from the end of the days of her flow and five from the beginning of the days of niddah. And she must complete two days for the days of niddah from the twelfth week, and she does not need seven clean days, since she saw only two days of the days of zivah.
the thirteenth week a zavah. It has six days of zivah and one day of niddah, and she becomes a zavah.
and the fourteenth week for counting. It has six days of niddah and one day of zivah.
the fifteenth week a zavah. It has seven days of zivah, and she becomes a zavah.
the sixteenth week for counting. It has three days of zivah and four days of niddah.
and the seventeenth week a zavah. It has three days of niddah and four days of zivah, and she becomes a zavah.
and the eighteenth week for counting. It has seven days of zivah. And after eighteen weeks she returns to the start of the cycle, and sees at the beginning of the days of her niddah.
has relations eighteen days. Seven days in the second week, six in the tenth week, and five in the twelfth week.
and she had a week of niddah and eleven days pure. For she used to see only in her days of niddah.
about a quarter of the days. Almost a quarter of the days on which she could have had relations if she had seen only in the days of niddah.

and this is what they said... she has relations a quarter of her days. And this does not mean a quarter of her lifetime, but a quarter of what she would have had relations if this illness had not befallen her.
watches one day for him... and has relations seven. For she did not become a zavah, since she saw only one day in the days of zivah.
and has relations seven a second time. For here too she did not become a zavah, since she saw only two days in her zivah.
in every forty-eight. But on the days afterward the calculation changes (see Maggid Mishneh).
and so on forever. For in every two ninths she returns to the start of the cycle, and to seeing at the beginning of the days of niddah.

her days of relations match the number of her zivah. At the start of her seeing, when there are seven days of niddah and the rest are the days of her zivah, and when she stops seeing there are seven clean days and the rest are for her relations. But in the other times in the cycle it is not necessarily calculated this way, since the days of niddah and zivah do not always correspond to the days of seeing.
there is a woman who has a cycle. There are women who have a cyclical pattern of seeing blood.

and there is a woman who has no cycle but does not feel herself until the blood comes out and has no fixed day for her seeing. There are women who have no physical symptoms and no fixed day for seeing blood.
and before the blood comes she feels herself yawning and sneezing. She will know that blood is about to come, according to bodily events.
and she feels in her abdomen and the lower part of her intestines. She feels heaviness in the bottom of her belly.
at a fixed hour for her from the day of her cycle. At a known time on that day (see also Hilchot Metamei Mishkav uMoshav 3:6).
she is forbidden to have relations until she first examines herself. And ensures that she is pure (above 4:16), because at any time she might become impure.
she is forbidden to have relations throughout the time of the cycle. Above 4:12-13.
and from the beginning of the day of the cycle she counts etc.. Above 6:6.
to be careful with cycles. To be precise and attentive to exactly when she sees.
her habit was. She was accustomed so, and a cycle was fixed for her when she saw so three times, as below.

both of them are forbidden. For the cycle that was fixed on the twentieth was not uprooted, because it was canceled only once, and she must be concerned for it. And she must likewise be concerned for the twenty-third, on which she last saw.
because of duress. Physical strain.
for she saw because of the duress. And not because of the days.
jumped. An example of duress.
for the day caused her to see, not the jumping. For she saw on the twentieth without having jumped on it, which proved that the day causes it and not the jumping.
she saw on the fifteenth of the month etc.. According to the date.
she has fixed a cycle by skipping. That each time the seeing is delayed by one day, and she is concerned for the eighteenth of the following month.

the fourth month came and she saw blood on the eighteenth, a cycle has not yet been fixed for her. This is the text in the manuscripts, and it appears corrupted (see the variants in the Frankel edition). The Maggid Mishneh cites a different reading: "she saw on the fifteenth... and the seventeenth of the following month and the eighteenth of the following month, she has fixed a cycle by skipping. The fourth month came and she saw on the seventeenth, a cycle has not yet been fixed for her." From this it follows that four sightings are needed to fix a skipping cycle, and if in the fourth month she saw without skipping, the cycle was not fixed.
and every day on which she saw, she is concerned for it in the future. Lest she see on that date.

and changed to the sixteenth, both are forbidden. For the cycle that was fixed on the fifteenth was not uprooted, because it was canceled only once, and she is still concerned for it. And she is likewise concerned for the sixteenth, on which she last saw.
and all were permitted. For the fixed cycle of the fifteenth was uprooted, because she did not see on it three times, and the others are canceled after one time.

a woman does not fix a cycle for herself within the days of her niddah in which she saw. For if she already saw in that same cycle of 'days of niddah', none of the following days can be fixed as the time of her cycle.
and likewise a woman does not fix a cycle in the days of her zivah. For even if she fixed a cycle then, it is uprooted after one time, as will be explained.
but she fixes a cycle in the days of her niddah in which she does not see. For she has not yet seen in them, and the day on which she sees will be the day of her cycle.
and if a cycle was fixed for her in the days of her zivah. That she saw on it three times.
she is concerned for the cycle. In the manner that will be explained in the next halakhah.
for the presumption is that blood is removed. In these days the woman is not supposed to see blood, and therefore even if she fixed a cycle, it is uprooted by one time of not seeing on it.
how is she concerned for the cycle. That was fixed in the days of her zivah.

if she saw blood in this cycle, even one day, she sits as a doubtful niddah. Even though she is in the days of her zivah, she must be stringent to be like a niddah, impure for seven days, because it came at her cycle (Maggid Mishneh).

and she is forbidden to have relations on that day even if she did not see on the other days of the cycles. She is forbidden to have relations in the future on that date, even if she did not see three times on that date but only once in the days of zivah. For concern for a cycle regarding the prohibition of relations is established after one time, as above halakhah 6 (Pardes Rimonim, Yoreh De'ah 184, Shach, subsection 19).

and if she saw three days she is a zavah. For despite the stringency above, that if she sees at such a cycle she is a niddah and impure all seven days, if she saw three days she is a zavah, and needs seven clean days.
who examines herself frequently. To ensure she did not become impure (and see above 4:16).
even if she has a fixed cycle. She too is praiseworthy, for there is benefit in it.
she sat and did not examine... she is in a presumption of purity. Even if the days of her zivah passed, we do not assume she became impure until it becomes known.
even though she is impure retroactively etc.. Although she is considered impure from the time of the cycle.
as will be explained regarding impurity and purity. Hilchot Metamei Mishkav uMoshav 3:5.

she does not make the one who has relations with her impure retroactively. For they made him impure with severe impurity only if she was already presumed a niddah, but he is considered only as one who touched a niddah (ibid. 3:8).
and she does not count. The seven days of impurity.
and if she found herself pure. After some time, she is in a presumption of purity, since it is reasonable that she did not see at the time of the cycle.
and likewise a woman who saw blood because of a wound she has in the source. That she has a sore in the womb which emits blood, and it is pure (and see above 4:20).
for cycles are by their decree. By rabbinic law, and therefore the time of the cycle itself does not make the seeing impure.
as will be explained in Hilchot Metamei Mishkav uMoshav. 3:9.
the blind woman. A blind woman, who cannot examine herself.
the deaf-mute woman and the imbecile. Who have no understanding (see Hilchot Ishut 2:26), and are not able to examine themselves (see also Hilchot Metamei Mishkav uMoshav 4:9).
women of sound mind. Ordinary women, who are not deaf-mutes or imbeciles (ibid.).
who erred and did not know the time of her cycle. Who does not know whether she is in her days of niddah or zivah.
is concerned for zivah. She is stringent to act also as a zavah, as will be explained.
perhaps this blood is in her days of niddah. To be stringent, whereas if it were in her days of zivah she would watch only one day.
to fix her cycle. That she establish anew the days of niddah and zivah, to get out of the doubt.
all according to the days on which she sees. The time of the fix varies according to the total days of her seeing, as will be explained below.
she completes the seven for them. She assumes she is in the days of niddah, which is the usual time for her to see, and is impure seven days.
and she begins counting the eleven days after the seven. And after them she returns to the start of the days of her niddah.
this is a doubtful zavah. And she is not a certain zavah, for it is possible she did not see three consecutive days in the days of zivah.
and sits five more to complete the days of niddah. For we assume that only one or two days were in the days of zivah, and the two remaining days were in the days of niddah.
and eleven days of zivah after the five. Making sixteen days in total.
this is a doubtful zavah. For it is not certain that she saw three consecutive days in the days of zivah.

perhaps two before the days of niddah and seven of niddah. For if she saw three days or more, we assume that no more than the first two days were of her days of zivah (and therefore she is not a certain zavah), and the days after that are of her days of niddah.
the three after the niddah. And they are of her days of zivah.
seven of her days of zivah will remain for her. For we assume she saw two days before her niddah and another seven days of niddah, and the four days after them are of her days of zivah.
she extended the seeing of blood. More than thirteen days.
and after the seven the days of niddah begin for this one who erred. For in these cases the days of seeing are not taken into account in the cycle, but her days of niddah begin anew.
until she feels and sees blood and it comes out in her flesh. Only if she knows with certainty that blood came out of the womb, and came out from it into the outer chamber.
as we have explained. Above 5:2.

and she will be impure only from the time she sees and onward. She became impure from the time of seeing the blood and onward, and we do not worry that perhaps the blood came and she became impure some time earlier.
this is presumed to have come with sensation. For its presumption is that it is from the chamber and impure.
as we have explained. Above 5:5.
and by the words of the scribes. By rabbinic enactment.
even though she did not feel. That she did not know that blood came out of her.
perhaps this stain came from the blood of the chamber. For there is concern that the blood is from the womb, and is impure.
not at the time of her cycle. Not at the time of the cycle fixed for her (see above 8:1-2).
impure retroactively up to twenty-four hours. She renders impure ritually pure items she touched during the entire last day (Hilchot Metamei Mishkav uMoshav 3:7-8).
as we have said. Above 8:13.
counts for her niddah. The seven days of her niddah.
or for her stain. The days required to become pure from the stain (see below halakhah 39).
and her cycle was spoiled. The fixing of cycles explained above 8:1-8.
one who sees blood at the time of her cycle. At the time fixed for her seeing (above 8:1-2).

a pregnant woman and a nursing woman... their moment is enough for them. They become impure only from the moment they see, for they are presumed not to see blood (and see also Hilchot Metamei Mishkav uMoshav 4:1-6).
once her pregnancy is recognizable. Once the pregnancy is noticeable.

all twenty-four months, even if her son died etc.. For twenty-four months from the birth, even if she does not actually nurse, for the lack of blood does not depend on nursing but on the birth itself.
a virgin, whoever has not seen blood in her life. Who has never yet seen niddah blood.
whoever ninety days have passed over her close to her old age. And she did not see blood in them.
and she is not particular. She does not get angry.
their stains are like their sightings. Their law is the same.
her stain is pure. For blood is not yet found in her, and there is no reason to assume that the blood on her is from her.
that she see blood three cycles. And then she is presumed to see niddah blood.
found on her flesh. On her actual body.
has no measure. And it defiles in any size (and its laws will be explained below halakhot 8-9).

like a Cilician gris that is square. A gris is a kernel split in two. This measure is measured with fava beans from the place called Cilicia, which are large and tend to be square-shaped (Commentary on the Mishnah, Negaim 6:1; and see Commentary on the Mishnah, Ma'aserot 5:7, Tosefta there 3:15). When the kernel is split in two lengthwise, its inner surface is flat and smooth and convenient for measuring.
drops. Drops, and not a single stain.
if it was long, it combines. If the stain is elongated, with an area like that of a Cilician gris.
an earthenware vessel from its back. From its outer side, from which it does not become impure (ibid. 13:1).
a garment that has not three fingerbreadths etc.. That is the minimum area of a garment to receive impurity (ibid. 22:1).
on something that does not receive impurity. A material that does not receive impurity.
stone vessels, earthen vessels and dung vessels. Which do not receive impurity in any way (Hilchot Kelim 1:6).
fish skin. It does not receive impurity, like anything that grows in the sea (ibid. 1:3).
opposite her private parts. Opposite the place of the genitals, from which blood comes.
her thigh and the inside of her feet. The inner part of her legs and the soles of her feet.
the tip of her big toe. The end of the toe on the foot.
the chamber. The source (above 5:3).
the joints of her fingers. The finger joints.
for hands are busy. They are accustomed to feel and touch the body, and it is reasonable that she touched the private parts.
on the outside or from the sides. Not on the inner side of the legs.
from the thighs and upward. Toward the upper half of the body, so it is reasonable that this is not blood that dripped from her private parts.
as if it were from below upward. It looks as if the blood flowed upward.
opposite her private parts she is impure. For the location itself arouses the suspicion, even if the shape of the stain is unusual.
from the belt and below. From the belt downward.
and above. Upward.
a sleeve. A sleeve.
she would take it off and cover herself with it. And so any part of it might be opposite the private parts.
the belt. The belt.
and remained in it. That she wore it without changing it for three consecutive days.
not at the time of her niddah. In the days of zivah.
perhaps a stain dripped from her each day. And if so she is a major zavah.
she wore three examined garments. One on top of the other.
even though this is opposite that. And one could have supposed that it is the same stain that passed from one garment to another.
