for betrothal does not take effect with forbidden relations. And we do not execute one who had relations with her, even though this too is a very slight doubt.

her father or brother was alive when her mother became pregnant with him. Perhaps the woman's father or brother is the father of that shetuki, and she is forbidden to him as his sister or his father's sister (above 2:3-5).

and every woman who was divorced or widowed. Perhaps her deceased or divorced husband was the father or the father's brother of the shetuki, and his wife is forbidden to him as a forbidden relation (above 2:1).

and from where do I say, etc.. Although the wife of an asufi is judged a doubtful married woman with regard to execution (above halachah 27), we do not forbid him in the first instance forbidden relations of kinship because of doubt.

for a fit person whose mother was examined, etc.. The first proof is that if a woman became pregnant through licentiousness, and was examined and said she was with a fit man, the law is that she is believed and her son is fit (above halachah 11), and he may marry any Israelite woman, and need not rule out entirely the possibility that she is his relative.
and behold it says, etc.. This is another proof.
for if this is done. If a person lets others have relations with his daughter without marriage.

the father is found marrying his daughter and a brother marrying his sister. As a result they will marry in violation of the prohibition, because they did not know they were relatives (see Hilchot Na'arah Betulah 2:17).
and if the law were... we would never have come to this measure. If forbidden relations of kinship were truly forbidden out of doubt, the same problem would not arise.
for if you say so. That indeed one must forbid marriage with everyone who might be a relative.
all the orphans in the world who did not know their fathers, etc.. Even if they are fully fit, they would have to be concerned about this, if they do not know who their father is.
lest they encounter a forbidden relation. They will marry someone who is a forbidden relation to them.
and someone came and said, "He is my son and I threw him out," he is believed. And he is established as his son, and not as an asufi.
since the name asufi went out about him. And he was established as unfit.
and in years of famine. Years of famine in the country.
for because of hunger they threw him out, etc.. It is reasonable that the parents are telling the truth.
who was swaddled. Wrapped in clothes.
who was salted. His body was cared for.
the kohl. Eye ointment.
amulets on his neck. Charms for protection against harmful spirits.
found under a dense tree that no animal enters. The branches block animals from entering there.
since they guard him so that he does not die, he is presumed fit. For if he were unfit, they would not leave him in a guarded place.
in the middle of the road. Where he could be trampled.
this is an asufi. It is evident that they did not care for his welfare, and it is reasonable that he is unfit.
a midwife. A birth attendant.
this child is a kohen. That the baby was born to the wife of a kohen.
because he was not established and we do not know his lineage. There is no other information, and she is the first to report anything about him.
fit, but he has no lineage. Fit to enter the congregation, but has no clear lineage.
because they are doubtful cases. And doubtful cases are forbidden to one another (above halachah 22).
definite mamzerim and Nethinim are permitted to enter one another. For the Nethinim are converts.
and the child is a mamzer... and the child is doubtful. For we follow the defective one (above halachot 7, 24).
one with crushed testicles and one with a severed organ. Whose sexual organs were injured, as will be explained below, 16:3-9.
and they are permitted to marry a convert and a freed woman. Who are not within the category of "congregation of the Lord" (see above 15:7).
even a kohen. Who is forbidden to a convert and freed woman when he is in his holiness (below 18:1).
he is permitted to marry a convert and freed woman who is not in his holiness. With regard to the marriage prohibitions of the priesthood, if he has crushed testicles.
the doubtful cases. Doubtful mamzer status (explained above in chapter 15).
they did not decree this regarding the Nethinim. Who are forbidden by the decree of King David (above 12:22-24).
nor regarding the doubtful cases. Against whom a prohibition was decreed (above 15:21-24).
for her prohibition is from the Torah. As opposed to the others mentioned in this halachah, whose prohibition is rabbinic.
the testicles. The testes.
the organ. The male organ.
and with three organs a male can father children. Procreation is possible only when these three organs are intact.
the testicular cords. The tubes that carry seed, passing between the testicles and the organ.
was wounded. Injured.
was severed. Cut from the body.
was crushed. Pounded.
the corona. The thickened part surrounding the tip of the organ.
above the corona. From the corona upward, toward the body.
from the head of the corona. The end farthest from the body.
like a hair's thread surrounding the whole organ. Some thickness of the corona remains, encircling the organ.
the organ was severed above the corona. A piece was cut from it, on the side toward the body.
like a quill. A cut on the side of the organ, like a writing reed cut diagonally.
like a gutter. A cut in a part of the sides of the organ, like a gutter carved only in the middle.
fit. These defects do not prevent the ability to father children.
if it was perforated above the corona, he is fit. Toward the body, for a perforation there does not harm the ability to father children (R. Y. Kapach).

perforated below the corona, with its opposite above, within the corona. The perforation is on the side of the tip of the organ, in a place that is below the corona, but on the other side it injures the corona itself.
for the whole corona is essential. And it must be complete.
the channel of seminal emission is blocked, etc.. The tube through which the seed leaves the body is blocked, and the seed comes out through the urinary tube.
that it was lacking. Part of it was missing.
one of the testicular cords was perforated into the urinary channel. And a passage of urine was created into the channel of seminal emission.
urinates from two places. Urine comes out of both tubes.
when they were not at the hands of Heaven. But were caused by direct injury.
who became ill from his own body. He had a disease, and it was not from physical injury.
shechin. A disease that damages the skin and nerve cells, and can cause parts of limbs to fall off as a result of infection.
and dissolved it. The shechin dissolves the organ.
for all these are at the hands of Heaven. They are included in this definition, and therefore are not within the category of crushed testicles or severed organ.
to destroy the organs of seed. To damage them, injuring them until their function stops.
from the oral tradition. The tradition of the Sages in interpreting the verses.

and the meaning of the verse "You shall not do this in your land". The meaning of the limitation "in your land" is that it is forbidden for Israelites to do this, and it is not a matter of place or land.
whether on their own bodies or on the bodies of others. It is forbidden to castrate Israelites or gentiles.
and anyone who castrates. Who damages the organs of seed.
one who castrates after a castrator receives lashes. For Scripture was inclusive: "crushed, beaten, torn or cut" (Leviticus 22:24).
torn. He did not cut them off entirely, but detached the inner parts.
and crushed. Smashed.
even though the latter castrated only one already castrated. Although after the first injury he was already castrated.
and one who castrates a female... is exempt. For she is not included in "crushed, beaten, torn or cut," etc.
akarin. A mixture of plants that causes sterility.
and one does not receive lashes for it. For the castration mentioned in Scripture relates to direct injury to the sexual organs.

and a woman is permitted... so that she does not give birth. In order not to give birth; since there are no lashes for castrating a female even through direct action (above halachah 11), and drinking akarin is indirect harm.
who tied. Bound him.
and set on. Provoked and incited the animal to attack him.
rebellion lashes. Lashes given to one who violates the words of the Sages.
our animal. That of an Israelite.
and if the gentile took it on his own. The gentile took the animal to castrate it of his own free will, without being asked.
and if the Israelite schemed in this matter. That the gentile took it himself to castrate it, but it was done on the Israelite's initiative.
we penalize him. So that the animal not remain in his ownership.
to another Israelite. For an Israelite may buy it, even though a transgression was committed with it.
to his adult son. Who is considered another person.
to his minor son he does not sell it or give it to him. Because all his property belongs to his father.
and a prostitute. A woman who had forbidden relations (her definition will be explained below in chapter 18).
and a chalalah. A woman who was disqualified from the holiness of the priesthood (her definition will be explained below 19:1-7).

whether a high priest anointed with the anointing oil or one invested with the garments. Whether a high priest anointed to the high priesthood with the anointing oil (see Hilchot Kelei HaMikdash 1:1-2), or appointed to the high priesthood by wearing the high priestly garments after the anointing oil ceased (there 1:12-13), their law is the same.

and whether a serving priest or a high priest who was appointed and was removed. Whether a high priest still serving in his post, or one removed from his post because of a blemish or old age, or one who was initially appointed to the high priesthood on a temporary basis.
and likewise a priest anointed for war. A priest appointed to address the people when going out to war (see Hilchot Melachim chapter 7).
are commanded regarding a virgin. To marry only a virgin.
one of the three women. A divorcee, a prostitute and a chalalah.
in the manner of licentiousness. Without betrothal and marriage.
they shall not take. This is the language of betrothal, and it was said regarding the prohibition of these three women.
because of "and he shall not profane". The verse said of the high priest: "and he shall not profane his seed among his people, for I am the Lord who sanctifies him."

for once he had relations with her he profaned her and disqualified her from the priesthood. Any woman forbidden to the priesthood who had relations with a kohen becomes a chalalah thereby (below 19:1), and a widow who had relations with a high priest is forbidden to every kohen as a chalalah.
but a prostitute... they are already profaned before his relations. For they were forbidden to all kohanim even before.
therefore he receives lashes... for he profaned her. By this relation she was profaned.

and he is warned not to profane fit ones, neither a woman nor his seed. Besides the prohibition of marrying forbidden women, the high priest has the added prohibition of causing fit persons to be profaned. Although it says "his seed," the prohibition applies both regarding a woman, whom he may not cause to become a chalalah, and regarding the sons and daughters he fathers from a forbidden relation.
because of "he shall not take a widow". This is a prohibition like the other priestly prohibitions: if he had relations after marriage he receives lashes (as above halachah 2).
because of "he shall not profane". Because he causes her to be forbidden to the other kohanim (as above halachah 3).
for there is no difference. No distinction.
except for a designated maidservant. Except in the case of one who had relations with a designated maidservant, where the man and the woman are not punished with the same punishment.
as we explained. Above 3:14.
she is not eligible for betrothal. Betrothal does not take effect with gentiles (Hilchot Ishut 4:15; Hilchot Gerushin 10:19).

and he is forbidden to have relations with a prostitute, whether Israelite or gentile. For even a gentile woman falls under the prohibition of prostitute (below 18:1), and since betrothal does not apply to her, he receives lashes for the act of relations alone (see also above 12:3).
the chalutzah. A yevamah for whom the brother-in-law performed chalitzah so that she may marry another (see Hilchot Yibbum VaChalitzah 1:1-2).
because she is like a divorcee. She resembles a divorcee in that she was bound in a marital bond to a particular man and was released from it during his lifetime.
rebellion lashes. Lashes for one who violates the words of the Sages.
a doubtful chalutzah. There was doubt whether she needed chalitzah.
and she is fit and her child is fit. They are not chalalim.
we give him rebellion lashes. We punish him for the doubt, by rabbinic enactment.
and he sends her out with a get. He must divorce her, because this is a doubt about a Torah prohibition.

for no prohibition takes effect upon another prohibition. An additional prohibition does not take effect on something already forbidden (see also Hilchot Shegagot 4:1), and he is punished only for the first prohibition.
if the two prohibitions came together. If both prohibitions took effect at once (for examples see above 2:1, Hilchot Ma'achalot Asurot 5:5, Hilchot Ma'aseh HaKorbanot 11:9).

if one prohibition added certain things to that prohibition. If the additional prohibition carries added stringency over the first (for examples see Hilchot Ma'achalot Asurot 14:18-19, Hilchot Terumot 10:25).

if it included other things together with this prohibition. If the prohibition applies to additional things that are otherwise permitted, including the forbidden thing (for examples see Hilchot Ma'achalot Asurot 7:2, 8:6).
since a widow is forbidden to a high priest, etc.. This explains how, in this order, each prohibition adds to the one before it.
she became a divorcee again. She married another and was divorced from him.
and became forbidden to an ordinary priest. Now another prohibition has been added, which is an "adding prohibition."
permitted to eat terumah. If her father is a kohen.
she became a chalalah. She had relations with a kohen and was thereby profaned.
she became forbidden to terumah. For a chalal is like a stranger in every respect (Hilchot Terumot 6:7), and this too is an "adding prohibition."
she became a prostitute. She had a forbidden relation.

since there is licentiousness that forbids a woman to an Israelite, etc.. There are cases in which a woman becomes forbidden to her husband through licentiousness, even if he is an Israelite and not a kohen (see Hilchot Gerushin 11:14); the prohibition of prostitution is therefore considered to add stringency, an "adding prohibition," and takes effect on the earlier prohibitions.
if this order were changed. So that no prohibition is added each time.
but only one for each act of relations. For there is only one prohibition in it.
a widow, whether from betrothal. Her husband died after the betrothal, before the marriage.

a high priest whose brother died. Without children, and he is obligated to perform yibbum with the wife, whereas he is forbidden to a widow (above halachah 3) and commanded to marry a virgin (below halachah 13).

even though she is from betrothal. Even if she is a widow from betrothal, who is presumed to be a virgin (see Hilchot Ishut 11:1), it is forbidden to perform yibbum with her (see Hilchot Yibbum VaChalitzah 6:10).

even though he made a ma'amar with her, etc.. Even if he performed the betrothal act that the Sages instituted for a yevamah, called ma'amar (there 2:1), she is not fully considered his wife, and it is forbidden to perform yibbum with her.
but if he betrothed the widow and was appointed high priest. In a case where an ordinary priest betrothed a widow, and afterward was appointed high priest.

this one may marry her. For this betrothal takes effect by Torah law, and he acquires her with a full acquisition. And of course if he was already married to a widow and was appointed high priest, he may keep her.
a doubtful widow. She is forbidden to a high priest as a doubtful case (see above halachah 7).

that he marry a virgin girl. That he marry specifically one of na'arah age, who has produced two hairs after age twelve; for six months from then she is called a na'arah, and afterward a bogeret (Hilchot Ishut 2:1-2).
a minor. Before age twelve.
and he does not marry two wives. That he not be married to two at the same time (see Hilchot Kelei HaMikdash 5:10), whereas other Israelites are permitted this (Hilchot Ishut 14:3).
struck by wood. Whose virginity was lost through injury and not through intercourse.
not in the natural manner. Through the rectum.
she is like one who had natural relations. This too is called relations for every purpose (see above 1:10).
with an animal, she is permitted. For this act is not considered the forbidding kind of relations (see below 18:1).
he does not receive lashes. Because he transgressed a positive commandment, and lashes are given only for negative commandments (Hilchot Sanhedrin 18:1).
he sends her out with a get. He must divorce her, and if he had relations with her she is profaned from the priesthood (below 19:3).
he may keep her. For they were not deflowered.
he may marry after he was appointed. For even a widow is permitted to him in such a case (above halachah 12).

raped a virgin girl or seduced her. He had relations with her against her will or with her consent. By Torah law the rapist and seducer must marry her, if she and her father wish (Hilchot Na'arah Betulah 1:1-3), but a high priest is forbidden to a non-virgin.
even if he raped or seduced her when he was an ordinary priest, etc.. Even if the obligation to marry arose when he was permitted to a non-virgin, he is not permitted.

because her body changed. To the state of a bogeret, who is forbidden to a high priest. She differs from one betrothed to a kohen who afterward was appointed high priest (above halachot 12, 15) in that her body changed.
and if he married her, he does not send her out. For one who married a bogeret may keep her (above halachah 15).
the one who refused. A minor orphan whose marriage is rabbinic, and who leaves her husband's authority if she refuses to continue living with him, and is not considered divorced.
as we explained in Hilchot Gerushin. 11:16.
and anyone who is not fit, etc.. Who is exempt from chalitzah and chalitzah was nevertheless performed for her (for those eligible for chalitzah see Hilchot Yibbum VaChalitzah chapter 6).
she is not disqualified from the priesthood. For this is not chalitzah in any respect. The same applies to one for whom chalitzah was performed in a way that was not proper at all (see there 4:26).
a rumor went out about him... and she sits under him and serves him. A report spread that this kohen had divorced his wife, though in fact they live together.
we do not send her out, etc.. For we do not worry about a rumor if it arose after the marriage.
and if she married another kohen, she must leave the second. If after the first one's death she married another kohen, we are concerned about that rumor, since it arose before their marriage.
her name went out in the city that she was betrothed and divorced. It was publicized that she was betrothed and divorced, and she is therefore forbidden to the priesthood.
as we explained in Hilchot Gerushin. 10:20.
a rumor that she is a chalutzah, we do not worry about it. Because the Sages did not forbid a woman who is possibly a chalutzah (above 5:7).
a rumor went out about a virgin that she is no longer a virgin, we do not worry about it. For we worry about a rumor only in matters that involve a public act, such as betrothal and divorce.
and she may marry even a kohen. For there is no concern about the matter at all, and it is understood that she is fit for a Yisrael as well.
the law of Moses and Jewish practice. Matters of halakhah and the customs of the daughters of Israel (see Hilchot Ishut 24:11-12).
on the testimony of a shameful matter. Circumstantial evidence of an act of harlotry (see ibid. 24:15).
only on clear testimony. And not because of a rumor or an estimate.
from oral tradition. The Sages' tradition of the interpretation of Scripture.
that the harlot mentioned in the Torah. In the context of the prohibition of marriage to a kohen (Leviticus 21:7, 21:14).
any woman who is not a daughter of Israel. Who was not born Jewish.
a prohibition that applies equally to all. A prohibition applying to all of Israel (and not a prohibition specific to the priesthood).
a chalal. One born from the marriage of a kohen with a woman forbidden to him, and likewise one whose father is a chalal (below 19:1, 19:14).
even though she is permitted to marry him. For there is no prohibition on the daughters of Israel marrying chalalim (see below 19:11).
a woman who was had by an animal, even though it is punishable by stoning. For it is a severe transgression (Hilchot Sanhedrin 15:10).
for she has not been had by a man. One forbidden to her (and see below 5:5, above 17:14, Hilchot Terumot 6:11).
and one who had relations with a niddah... she is not forbidden to marry him. Although this is a forbidden relation, there is no prohibition of marriage here.
one who has relations with an unmarried woman. A single woman, without betrothal.
a kedeshah who made herself available to all. One set aside and given over to harlotry.
it is punishable by lashes. For it is a prohibition of a negative commandment (Hilchot Ishut 1:4).
one of the negative prohibitions that apply equally to all. Such as a mamzer and a natin (see in the next halakhah, and Hilchot Ishut 1:7-8).
of the prohibitions of positive commandments. An Egyptian or Edomite convert (see ibid.).
on account of a forbidden relation. A prohibition punishable by karet (Hilchot Ishut 1:5).
or to a gentile or a slave. For betrothal does not take effect with them either (see above 12:3).
even if she converted or was freed when she was younger than three years. That she converted before she was fit for intercourse (above 1:13).
from here they said. From the principle explained until now.
a natin or a mamzer... or one with crushed testicles or a severed organ. For all of these are prohibitions of negative and positive commandments.
a kohenet who was disqualified from terumah. For the daughter of a kohen who became a chalalah is forbidden to eat terumah (Hilchot Terumot 6:7).

a yevamah with whom a stranger had relations. One who is not her husband's brother; she is forbidden to marry him until her husband's brothers perform chalitzah for her (Hilchot Yibbum VeChalitzah 2:18).
and an ayelonit. A woman whose sexual development is defective and who cannot bear children (Hilchot Ishut 2:6).

is permitted to a kohen and is not a harlot. For there is no inherent prohibition in marrying an ayelonit, except for a man who has not fulfilled the commandment to be fruitful and multiply (see ibid. 15:7).
the secondary relatives. Female relatives forbidden by rabbinic enactment (for the details see Hilchot Ishut 1:6).
and the like. Additional women forbidden to marry by rabbinic enactment.
a relative of his chalutzah. For the relatives of a chalutzah are forbidden to the one who performed chalitzah by rabbinic enactment, as if they were relatives of his wife.
or with his chalutzah. For even the widow of his brother, after he performed chalitzah for her, is forbidden to him by rabbinic enactment.
as we explained in Hilchot Yibbum. 1:12-13.
as will be explained. Below 19:11.
and she becomes a harlot. And she is forbidden to a kohen (as above 5:1).
only through a defect. Through a relation that carries a defect, with a man forbidden to her, and not through the forbidden act itself.
and from oral tradition. In the tradition of the Sages.
as we explained. Above chapters 1-4.
in an unnatural manner. From behind.
once he has begun entry. For the definition of begun entry see above 1:10.
a girl of three years and one day... a boy of nine years and one day. For then they are fit for intercourse (above 1:13).
whether by force or willingly, she is disqualified from the priesthood. For this is a forbidden relation.
he is flogged on her account for defilement. As with a married woman who committed adultery willingly.

her first husband... cannot take her back. The continuation of the verse: "after she has been defiled." From this they learned that a married woman who had a forbidden relation with another man is forbidden to her husband by a negative commandment (Hilchot Gerushin 11:14).
everything is included, etc.. The verse includes all women who had a forbidden relation.

Scripture specified for you regarding the wife of a Yisrael, etc.. Regarding the wife of a Yisrael, Scripture states explicitly that she is not forbidden to him if she was raped, but only if she committed harlotry willfully.
and she was not seized. When she was not raped she is forbidden, and if she was raped she is permitted; this law applies only to the wife of a Yisrael (Hilchot Ishut 24:19).
but the wife of a kohen... for she is a harlot. For she had a relation with someone she is forbidden to marry, and therefore the prohibition of defilement applies to her.
she is forbidden to the priesthood. Because she had a forbidden relation. And if her husband dies she is forbidden to marry a kohen.

she is not forbidden to him, perhaps she set her eyes on another. A woman who says she had a forbidden relation is not believed, because we suspect that she invented the matter to force her husband to divorce her, so that she could marry another. Likewise, one witness is not believed to forbid a woman to her husband.
she is believed... he is believed. He believes them (see also Hilchot Ishut 24:17-18, 24:23).
as we explained. In the previous halakhah.
she is forbidden to every kohen in the world. To other kohanim, as a harlot.
she admitted. She admitted it.
and she becomes like a forbidden piece of meat. Like something forbidden in itself, for a person is believed to forbid himself by his own admission (see above 13:8, Hilchot Gerushin 12:1-3).
an adult or a minor. For in this law there is no difference between an adult and a minor (compare below halakhah 11).

and some time later he had relations with her and claimed that he found her not a virgin. That some time passed after the betrothal until he had relations with her, and he discovered that she had been had by a man.

perhaps she was had before the betrothal, etc.. For there is a doubt whether she was had when she was unmarried, in which case she is not forbidden to him, or whether she was had after the betrothal, when she was already a married woman, and is forbidden as a harlot.
as we explained. Above 5:7.
if her father betrothed her. In this case the betrothal takes effect by Torah law even for a minor (Hilchot Ishut 3:11).
and she is younger than three years and one day. For even if she had a relation before then, her virginity returns (ibid. 11:3).
and he claimed. The husband, after the marriage.
for there is only one doubt here. For she was found not to be a virgin, and certainly she was had after the betrothal.
and a doubt about a Torah prohibition is resolved stringently. See the rule in Hilchot Mamrim 1:5.

any woman whose husband warned her and she secluded herself. That her husband warned her not to be alone with a man and she was afterward alone with him, and thereby she is forbidden to her husband until she drinks the sotah waters to determine whether she committed adultery (Hilchot Sotah 1:1-2).
a possible harlot. For without drinking the waters it was not clarified whether she committed adultery.
that she did not want to drink, whether he did not want. For in these situations she is not made to drink (ibid. 2:1).
testimony that prevented her from drinking. That one witness testifies that she committed adultery, and she is forbidden to drink (ibid. 1:14).
that the court warned her. That if the husband is unable to warn, the court warns in his place, but she is not made to drink (ibid. 1:10-11).
the women who are not fit to drink. See ibid. 2:2.
and he went away. And there is no way to determine who he is, and whether he disqualifies her by his relation.
and she said, a fit man. One who is not disqualified in lineage.
she is believed. And she is fit for the priesthood (and see above 15:11).
a crossroads. A meeting of roads.
at the corners of the field. Outside the city.
a stringency in matters of lineage. A stringency in matters of lineage and marital ties (for further examples see above 13:10, 15:21).
two majorities. That the majority of those passing the place are fit, and likewise the majority of the people of the city from which those passing came out.
and if she married she need not leave. For this is only a stringency in matters of lineage, and by strict law her statement that she had relations with a fit man suffices.
they saw her having relations in the city. And not outside it.

for anything fixed in place is like half and half. For each side of a doubt that is fixed in its place is considered an equal factor to the opposing side of the doubt, and we are concerned about it even if it is small (for this rule see Hilchot Chametz UMatzah 2:10).
she was mute, etc.. And there is no possibility that she would say that she had relations with a fit man (and see above 15:12).
the two majorities. As above, halakhah 14.
the captive woman. A woman captured by gentiles, where there is a concern that she had relations with a gentile.
and she is three years and one day old. For before that her relations are not considered relations (above 1:13), and she is not disqualified from the priesthood by them.
even a slave, a woman, or a relative. Who are generally disqualified from testifying (Hilchot Edut 9:1).

and two captive women, each of whom testified for her fellow, are believed. For a woman is believed in this testimony, and we do not suspect that each of them lies in return for the testimony of her fellow.

since the prohibition of all doubts is rabbinic. And this includes the prohibition of the captive woman, so they were lenient about it (and see further examples in Hilchot Kilayim 10:27, Hilchot Tumat Met 9:12).
speaking innocently. Speaking without intending to testify.
and my mind was on my mother. And I was not separated from her at all.
the husband. The kohen.
her maidservant may not testify for her. For her maidservant might lie for her benefit.
perhaps he had his eye on her. For we suspect that he lied and testified that she is pure because he wanted to marry her.
and if he redeemed her and testified for her. The kohen is the one who redeemed her from captivity, for payment.
for had he not known that she is pure, etc.. That unless he had first clarified that she is pure, he would not have spent his money to redeem her.

for the mouth that forbade is the mouth that permitted. Just as we rely on her words to regard her as a captive, so we believe her that she is pure. (For this principle see above 13:10, Hilchot Gerushin 12:1.)
even if there was one witness there. As long as there is no testimony that she was a captive, other than her own words.
until one testifies for her that she is pure. For one witness suffices (above halakhah 17).
testifies that she was defiled. That she had relations with a gentile.
she is permitted. Because in the law of the captive woman they were lenient (above halakhah 17, and below 23).
and the court permitted her to marry. As stated in the previous halakhah.
she may marry from the outset and need not leave her permission. For she has already been permitted.
even if the captor entered after her. That immediately after her came the one who captured her, to the court, and the judges are thus witnesses that she was captured.
and we guard her from now until she is redeemed. That from that time onward we take care that she be guarded so that she does not have a forbidden relation.
she must leave. For it became clear through valid testimony that the permission was given in error.
for regarding the captive woman they were lenient. And therefore we are not careful at the outset to clarify the facts with witnesses, but are satisfied with what is before the court.
and she is a minor. If she is still a minor (see Hilchot Ishut 3:11, 9:10).
he is not believed to hold her as divorced. For she is no longer in his domain.
as it is said, "I gave my daughter," etc.. From this verse they learned that a father is believed to forbid her on account of marriage.
but not to disqualify her for harlotry. For he is not believed in this by Torah law.

she is permitted to live with him in one courtyard. Although there is some concern that they may come to sin. Unlike a kohen who divorced his wife, who are forbidden to live together even in the same alley (see below 21:27).
always to guard him. That he not be alone with her.
until they see her and it is done in their domain. So that if she tries to flee they will see her and catch her.
except one who was three years old or less. Besides these, whose relations are not considered relations.
as we explained. Above halakhah 17.
and they did not know about her. That they did not notice that she escaped.
her hiding place. A place of concealment.
holds only one. For the hiding place has room for only one.
since she could say, I escaped, etc.. We believe her that she is pure, for had she wanted to lie she would have claimed that she escaped or hid, and she would have been believed.
that kingdom. The government of that country.
for they settle in the city and are not afraid. That they do not fear that another army will come to fight them.
another kingdom. The government of another place.
that spread, flooded, and passed through. That conquered the city.
for they busy themselves with the spoils and flee. Out of fear of the local army.
and if women were taken captive, etc.. We are not lenient with another government if women were taken captive and came into their domain.
who was imprisoned. Locked up.
over money. For a monetary reason.
and over capital matters. On an accusation carrying the death penalty.
for the hand of Israel is strong over the gentiles and they fear them. For the gentiles fear Israel, and therefore they will guard a woman imprisoned over money.
once she came into the domain of gentiles she became forbidden. For they are not careful to guard her.
as we explained. Above halakhah 17.
who was born from forbidden priestly marriages. From a marriage of a kohen with one of the women forbidden to the priesthood (for the details see above 17:1).
one of the women... became a chalalah. And she is now forbidden to a kohen even by the prohibition of a chalalah (see above 17:10).
but the kohen himself who committed the transgression did not become a chalal. For the sanctity of the priesthood does not leave him (see Hilchot Bi'at HaMikdash 6:9).
whether she was had by force, etc.. As with any relation that disqualifies among kohanim (above 18:6).
with a divorcee or a harlot. Those forbidden to him (above 17:1).
or with a widow. Forbidden only to the High Priest (above 17:3).

who married a non-virgin and had relations with her. That she becomes a chalalah only if she married him (see above 17:15), because her prohibition is learned from the commandment "and he shall take a wife in her virginity" (Leviticus 21:13), and if he violated it he profaned her.
the child is a chalal. Who was born of the marriage of a kohen with a woman forbidden to him.
a kohen who betrothed, etc.. And there was no marriage.
she was not profaned. Because she had not yet had relations, as above.
for every married woman is presumed to be a non-virgin. For so we assume in every case (Hilchot Ishut 11:1-2).
a bogeret. One for whom six months have passed since she became a na'arah (above 17:13).
one struck by wood. Whose virginity was lost through an injury and not through intercourse (above 17:14).
who married a bogeret or one struck by wood did not profane her. And he is even permitted to keep them (above 17:15).
had relations with a non-virgin without marriage did not profane her. For the non-virgin is forbidden to him only in marriage, as in the previous halakhah.
one of the forbidden relations. Those forbidden by karet (above, in the list of commandments at the beginning of this section of halakhot, commandments 1-22).
except for a niddah. Who is permitted to marry him.
of those liable under negative commandments that apply equally to all. Who are forbidden to all of Israel (for the details see Hilchot Ishut 1:7).
as we explained. Above 18:1-2.
a second act of intercourse. Another time, after he made her a harlot through the first act of intercourse.
she becomes a chalalah and his offspring from her are chalalim. From then on; before that she is not a chalalah.

a kohen who had relations with a woman awaiting yibbum. A yevamah waiting for yibbum or chalitzah from her husband's brothers, who is forbidden to marry a stranger (Hilchot Yibbum VeChalitzah 2:18), and a stranger who is a kohen had relations with her.
a convert and a freed slave. Who are not daughters of Israel (above 18:1), and are treated as harlots forbidden to the priesthood.

for the prohibition of a niddah is not specific to kohanim but applies equally to all. And therefore there is no law of chalal here. And she does not become a harlot through this relation, because she is permitted to marry him (and see above 18:1).
whether from him. That she conceived while married to him, and he divorced her and took her back.
did not come from a drop of transgression. That the child was not conceived in transgression, since she conceived before they married in violation.
we already explained. Above 17:7.
by their word. By decree of the Sages, and not by Torah law.

a prohibition that applies equally to all and is not specific to kohanim. And it carries no law of chalalut. And she does not become a harlot through this relation, since it is a rabbinic prohibition.
a doubtful convert or freed slave. For it is doubtful whether they are daughters of Israel or were born gentile (see an example above 12:15-16).
a doubtful divorcee. Whose betrothal was in doubt and she was divorced, or who was divorced in doubt.
a doubtful widow. Who was betrothed in doubt, and whose husband died (above 17:12).
there are three kinds of chalalim. Of three types.
the stringencies of kohanim and the stringencies of Yisraelim. That one must be stringent in both directions, for perhaps he is a kohen and perhaps he is a Yisrael.
he is like a stranger. For no law of the priesthood applies to him at all.

speak to the kohanim, the sons of Aaron. And later in the passage the laws of the kohanim are detailed: the prohibition of becoming defiled to the dead, the prohibition of marrying a harlot, a chalalah, or a divorcee, and eating terumah.
even though they are sons of Aaron, until they are in their priesthood. For the sons of Aaron are not commanded in the laws of the priesthood if they were removed from the sanctity of the priesthood.
as we explained. Above 18:3.
but a kohenet. The daughter of a kohen.
for they were not warned, are fit to marry the disqualified. For there is no restriction upon their marriages.
a convert is permitted to marry a mamzeret and is permitted to marry a kohenet. For he may marry from all levels of lineage.
who married one another. Without having mixed with Israelites.
that daughter is forbidden to a kohen. For her law is that of a convert (and see above 15:8).
and her conception. Her formation in her mother's womb.
in holiness. In the holiness of Israel, after both her parents converted.
his daughter is fit for the priesthood from the outset. For she is like a Yisraelit in every respect (see above 15:9).
a second-generation Egyptian. Whose parents were Egyptians who converted.
even though their relation was a transgression. For they are forbidden to enter the congregation (above 12:18-19).
as we explained. Above 18:3.

their daughters are fit. For they are not chalalot, since they were not born of a forbidden priestly marriage, and likewise the daughter of an Ammonite or an Egyptian convert in the third generation is permitted to enter the congregation.
his offspring from her are chalalim. For in the lineages of Israel the child follows the male (as below, halakhot 15-16).
a Yisrael who married a chalalah, the child is fit. For we follow the male.
they are permitted to marry one another. These to those.

for it is said, "and they declared their ancestry by their families, by their fathers' houses". From this verse, said regarding the census of Israel in the wilderness, we learn that each person is attributed to his father's family.
his father's house is his family. For lineage is determined by the father.
the son is a Yisrael. And he is forbidden to a mamzeret (above 15:9), and the daughter is permitted to the priesthood (above halakhah 12).
and it is permitted to marry from them from the outset. Without investigation.
who constantly provoke one another. Who quarrel all the time.
strife and quarrel. A dispute.
and brazen. Insolent.
are kinds of disqualification. Signs indicating a disqualification of lineage.
anyone who disqualifies others. Who curses them and says they are disqualified in lineage.
who casts a blemish. Who casts aspersions.
perhaps he is a Gibeonite. Those disqualified from entering the congregation (see above 12:22-24).
and the Gibeonites are not of the children of Israel. For they lack the good traits of the children of Israel (see also Hilchot Teshuvah 2:10).
and the sons of Saul did not show mercy. For they sought to kill them in revenge for Saul having killed among the Gibeonites (see II Samuel 21:1-14).
and they showed them kindness and let them live at first. For the Israelites made a covenant with the Gibeonites and protected them even after their deception was discovered (see Joshua chapter 9).
over whom a challenge was raised. A reputation went out about her that she is disqualified.
she is a doubtful case. And one may not marry from them from the outset without investigation.
four mothers who are eight. Four groups of mothers, who are eight women.
to examine one pair. In the generations above them.

for the mixture among Levites and Israelites is greater than among kohanim. The chance that a disqualification will have mixed in among them is greater, since kohanim are very careful about their lineage.
curses. Reviles.
and had there been a disqualification there, it would have been heard. For had there been any disqualification in his lineage, it would have come to light in the course of a quarrel.
for fit women were not warned against marrying the disqualified. The disqualified of the priesthood.
and is silent. Who does not protest.
a natin. From the seed of the Gibeonites.
we are concerned about him and his family. That perhaps this disqualification is indeed found among them.
as we explained. Above halakhah 18.

any widow of that family is forbidden to a kohen from the outset. For the wife of a chalal becomes a harlot (above 18:1), and regarding every widow of theirs there is a doubt whether she is the wife of the chalal.
two doubts. That even on the prohibited side of the doubt there is a further doubt (for this principle see above 18:10).
for the wife of a mamzer. Becomes a harlot.
as we explained. Above 18:3.
nowadays. In our times.
by presumption they are kohanim. That they are held and known as kohanim, but there is no certainty about it.
in the holy things of the border. Priestly gifts that are holy and eaten throughout the borders of the Land of Israel: terumah, terumat ma'aser, and challah.
terumah by rabbinic law. That they are obligated in it by rabbinic enactment (see below halakhah 3).
and he is the kohen who served on the altar. For he is certainly a kohen of established lineage.
for had the Great Court not examined, etc.. For the court would examine the lineage of every kohen before he began to serve in the Temple (Hilchot Bi'at HaMikdash 6:11).
we do not examine from the altar upward. For there is no need to examine the lineage of one who offered on the altar, for certainly he was examined before he was allowed to ascend and he is a kohen.
nor from the Sanhedrin upward. For one should not examine the lineage of one appointed to the Sanhedrin, for certainly he was examined before they appointed him (Hilchot Sanhedrin 2:1-2).
challah... is not by Torah law. Rather the obligation in it is by rabbinic enactment.
for it is said, "when you come to the land". Regarding the commandment of separating challah.

and when they went up in the days of Ezra, not all of them went up. When Israel returned from Babylonia to the Land of Israel, at the beginning of the Second Temple period, only part of the people came, and therefore they were not obligated by Torah law to separate challah even in the places they conquered (see also Hilchot Bikkurim 5:5).
and so too terumah nowadays. For regarding it too there is a similar exposition (see Hilchot Terumot 1:26).
who used to eat terumah by Torah law. At the time when it applies by Torah law.
and we do not elevate to lineage. To regard him as a kohen of established lineage.
from the raising of the hands. In which the kohanim bless the people (Hilchot Tefillah 14:3).
from reading from the Torah first. For this is the privilege of the kohanim (ibid. 12:18).
from the division of terumah at the threshing floors. The division of terumah at the grain threshing floor, where the kohanim receive the terumah (Hilchot Terumot 12:17).
and not on the word of one witness. Rather on two (as above halakhah 2), for complete certainty is needed in matters of lineage.
we do not elevate him. For his testimony is not enough to hold him as his son for this purpose (and see further in the next halakhah, and below halakhah 10).
for we knew that she is fit. That from the start it was clear that she is fit to marry into the priesthood.
clinging after her. Attached to her, as children are to their mothers.
he need not bring witnesses. For the woman was established as fit, and from the fact that the children cling after her it is evident that they are hers (see above 1:20).
he must bring witnesses that these are his sons. And the sons of that woman.
he must bring witnesses that this woman is fit. For her status was not known until now.
and he does not bring witnesses that these are her sons, etc.. For he need not, as in the previous halakhah.
he must bring proof about them. That they are his sons from the fit woman.
he brings witnesses that that woman was fit and that these are her sons. For testimony is required both about the woman and about her sons.
as a Yisrael of established lineage. That there is no disqualification in his family.
fit for the Sanhedrin. For only those of established lineage sit there (above halakhah 2).
in documents. From names written in documents.
we do not hold this kohen to be of established lineage. Even though there are two witnesses who apparently signed that he is a kohen.
perhaps they testified only about the loan. That their testimony does not refer to the lineage of the people but to the event of the loan. And in a matter of lineage, clear testimony is required.
but for presumption... we elevate from documents, etc.. For all of these are clear signs of priesthood.
to feed him terumah. By rabbinic law.
and he need not bring proof about the sons or about the woman. There is no need to prove that the mother is fit for the priesthood, and that the son is hers (and compare above halakhah 5).
even though they appear to be repaying one another. Although it seems that each testifies in favor of the other in return for his testimony about him.
and both are presumed to be kohanim. For each of them has one witness.
who divided at the threshing floor. Who received a share in the division of terumah at the grain threshing floor.
who divided with his brothers in court the terumah that their father left them. That they divided among themselves terumah they received as an inheritance from their father.

perhaps he is a chalal who took his inheritance share of terumah in order to sell it. For this is no proof that he is a kohen, because he may be a chalal, who is forbidden to eat terumah, and takes his inherited share intending to sell it to a kohen.
he forbids himself. He must be stringent on himself, since he regarded himself as a kohen.
and if he married or became defiled he is flogged. For he held himself to be a kohen.
a possible chalalah. And she is disqualified from the priesthood, for perhaps his words are true and he is a kohen.
one who speaks innocently is believed. One who speaks without intending to testify.
I remember. I recall.
and he stripped me of my shirt and immersed me to eat terumah in the evening. For kohanim eat terumah in a state of purity, and need nightfall after immersion (Hilchot Terumot 7:1-2).
keep their distance. They distance themselves, so as not to defile him.
our holy Rabbi. Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi.
an adult is believed to say, etc.. Although he testifies about what he saw when he was a minor and was not fit to testify.
perhaps he is a chalal. For testimony about the father does not help regarding the son, since it is possible that the son was born to a disqualified mother and became a chalal.
but if his father was established as a kohen... he is presumed like his father. For we follow presumption as long as no concern of disqualification is known.
and a rumor went out about him, etc.. A rumor spread that he is disqualified.
and they demote him. From the status of the priesthood.
one witness came... we elevate him. For one witness suffices to hold him as a kohen (above halakhah 11).
both these and those are set aside. Because the testimonies contradict one another they cancel each other, and we follow the presumption.

and the rumor is set aside, for two are like a hundred. In testimony the law is that the number of witnesses is not significant, only the testimony itself (see Hilchot Edut 18:3). Therefore we do not regard the rumor as an addition to the disqualifying testimony so as to decide in its favor, for the qualifying testimony stands against them.

a woman who did not wait three months after her husband. For the Sages instituted that a woman must wait a period between divorce or widowhood and marriage, so that if she is pregnant it will be known who the father of the child is (Hilchot Gerushin 11:18).
the child of a kohen got mixed with the child of a Yisrael. So that it is not known which is which.
the stringencies of Yisrael and the stringencies of kohanim. For one must be stringent in both possibilities.
and it is not known. That the child is certainly a kohen, but it is not known who his father is.
we apply to the child the stringencies of both. In matters of the priesthood, as will be explained.
an onen. One mourning on the day of death (Hilchot Ma'aser Sheni 3:6), who is forbidden on that day to perform Temple service (Hilchot Bi'at HaMikdash 2:6).
he is an onen for them and they are onenim for him. For we are concerned that he may be their relative, and he is forbidden to serve on the day of death.
he does not become defiled for them, etc.. For they are kohanim, who may become defiled only for their relatives (Hilchot Evel 2:6-15), and perhaps he is not their relative.
in his watch. The priestly families were divided into twenty-four watches, and each week a different watch served in the Temple (see Hilchot Kelei HaMikdash 3:9).
and he does not share. For his belonging to the watch is in doubt, and he has no certain right to the watch's offerings.
and the father's house. The watch was made up of several priestly families, called "father's houses," each of which served in the Temple on a different day of that week.
he takes one share. For he certainly has a share in the offerings of that day.
when they come by way of marriage. The children of doubt were born to a woman who was married to a kohen.
but through harlotry. That she had relations with a kohen without marriage, and it is not known who the father is.
for they silence him from the law of the priesthood. As will be explained below.
until his offspring is of established lineage after him. Clearly.
that one of them separated. From the group, so that it is certainly one of them.
they silence him. They prevent him.
from the law of the priesthood. From these rights of the priesthood.
he is flogged, for there is no doubt of permission here. Because he is certainly a kohen.
a forbidden relation of all the forbidden relations. Those forbidden by karet (for the details see above 1:4-7 and in the list of commandments at the beginning of this section of halakhot).
one who... by way of limbs. Who lay with her and rubbed against her other limbs, but did not have relations with her in a manner considered intercourse (see above 1:10).
and derives pleasure from bodily contact. In contact with the forbidden woman.
is flogged by Torah law. For even these acts are forbidden by a negative commandment.
"do not approach" things that lead to uncovering nakedness. The Torah forbade even acts that lead to a forbidden relation.

suspected of forbidden relations. And he is flogged for this transgression (see Hilchot Sanhedrin 19:4), and therefore he is also disqualified from testifying, since he committed a transgression punishable by lashes (Hilchot Edut 10:2).
to wink with his hands and feet. To signal and hint.
to joke. To laugh.
to act lightheaded. To engage in matters of foolishness.
and one who intends such a thing is given lashes for rebelliousness. For this involves excessive closeness to the severe prohibition of forbidden relations.
in the place of the nakedness. The place of the nakedness.
even to hear the voice of a forbidden woman or to look at her hair is forbidden. For even these lead to pleasure.
forbidden by negative commandments. Also with prohibitions that are not punishable by karet (see Hilchot Ishut 1:7).
in front of an unmarried woman and to examine her. Whether she is pleasing to him so that he will marry her.
rather it is proper to do so. To examine the woman before marriage, whether she is pleasing to him, so that she not become repulsive to him after the marriage (see also ibid. 3:19).
in the manner of harlotry. Not for the sake of marriage.
"I made a covenant with my eyes; how then could I look upon a virgin". From this praise we learn that looking at an unmarried woman is improper conduct.
to look at his wife when she is a niddah. To gaze at her when she is forbidden to him.
since she will be permitted to him after a time, etc.. When she becomes pure, and therefore there is less concern that they will come to transgress.
but he may not joke... lest he become accustomed to a matter of sin. For if they behave lightly, they may come to have relations during the time of the prohibition.
to be served by a woman. For personal service.
a freed slave. A maidservant who was freed and converted.
lest he come to improper thoughts. Of sin and harlotry as a result of the service.
for only his wife does these things for a man. For these are among the tasks that a wife does for her husband (Hilchot Ishut 21:3).
for a person's heart does not trouble him about them. He does not worry that he will come to sin because of contact with them.
this is most disgraceful. For it involves forbidden closeness to forbidden relations.
and she may sleep with him in bodily contact. They are permitted to sleep together without a garment between them.
as long as they are minors... "breasts have formed and your hair has grown". Until they reach an early stage of physical maturity (see also Hilchot Keriat Shema 3:19).
this one sleeps in his garment and that one sleeps in his garment. Each one must be covered with his own garment.
is ashamed to stand naked before her father. Even though she has not reached maturity.
or who has married. And she is a married woman.
to be ashamed. To feel shame.
who rub against one another. Who rub against one another in the manner of intercourse.
for it has no specific negative commandment. For the act was not explicitly forbidden, but is included in the category of "the practice of the land of Egypt."
there is no intercourse at all. There is no act of intercourse in this conduct.
they are not forbidden to the priesthood on account of harlotry. For harlotry applies only with intercourse (see above 18:3).
and a man should be strict with his wife in this matter. It is proper for a man to guard his wife against such conduct.
whatever he wishes to do with his wife, he does. For by law there are no restrictions on their conduct.
and that he sanctify himself at the time of intercourse. That is, that he act in a dignified manner fitting for a holy people.
as we explained in Hilchot De'ot. 5:4-5.
and he should not deviate from the way of the world and its practice, etc.. For it is proper to have relations only in the natural manner, which is the way of procreation.
by the light of a lamp. For this involves a lack of modesty.
and he had no other house. Another room without a lamp.
for it is brazenness. Insolence.
for he does not come to be drawn into it. That he is not liable to become accustomed to these acts.
darkens with his cloak. Makes it dark by means of a garment.
and the practice of boors. The custom of fools (for a list of the drawbacks of this see Hilchot De'ot 4:19).

provided that he not suspend conjugal relations except with his wife's knowledge. That a husband may not break his obligation to his wife regarding her conjugal rights, except with her consent (see Hilchot Ishut 15:1).

and the Sages originally did not institute for those who have had emissions, etc.. The reason the Sages originally instituted immersion for those who have had an emission before engaging in Torah and prayer was to cause fewer marital relations (Hilchot Keriat Shema 4:8, Hilchot Tefillah 4:4). Although this enactment was abolished, the principle for which it was established is still true.
and his mind is on another woman, etc.. For these things are exceedingly disgraceful.
against her will. Not willingly.
who resolved in his heart to divorce her. Who decided to divorce her.
the children are not worthy. The children born of this union may be defective.
for she demands intercourse with her mouth. Who demands intercourse explicitly and not by hinting.
one who entices a woman for the sake of marriage. And has relations with her before they marry.

who did not wait after her husband. That after she was divorced or widowed she did not wait, before marrying another, a period sufficient to determine who is the father of the fetus (see Hilchot Gerushin 11:18).
the children born of them are the rebellious and the transgressors. For even from these unions defective children are born.
for the sufferings of exile purge them. They destroy them and remove them from the community of Israel.
in the markets and streets, or in gardens and orchards. In public places (for the baseness of the act see Hilchot Sanhedrin 24:4).
and one who betroths without matchmaking. Without prior agreement, for these things are similar to harlotry (Hilchot Ishut 3:21-22).
a guest. A visitor.
to live in his father-in-law's house, for this is brazenness. For this is not within the bounds of modesty.

and likewise a person should not enter the bathhouse with his father, etc.. All this is out of modesty and also out of respect (and regarding respect for one's teacher see also Hilchot Talmud Torah 5:6).
with uncovered heads in the marketplace. Without a head covering conforming to the custom of their place (see Hilchot Ishut 24:12, 13:11).
and a woman should not walk in the marketplace with her son behind her. Without supervision over him.
a decree lest they seize her son. For such an incident occurred, and therefore they decreed this.
threshes inside and winnows outside. Has relations with the woman and emits the seed outside her body.
and he should not marry a minor who is not fit to bear a child. For he thereby nullifies the commandment of being fruitful and multiplying (Hilchot Ishut 15:7; and see ibid. 3:19).
who commit adultery with the hand. Acts of self-gratification.
for one who does this sits under a ban. A decree of separation from Israel in various matters (see Hilchot Talmud Torah 7:4).
and it is as if they killed a person. For that seed was destined to become a child.
that he make himself hard. He deliberately causes an erection of the male organ, and one is placed under a ban for this (Hilchot Talmud Torah 6:14).
improper thought. A thought of harlotry.
should turn his heart away from words of vanity and corruption. Should turn his thoughts from these matters, which are foolish talk, to words of Torah.
on his neck... until he tilts slightly. When he lies on his back, rather he must turn slightly to the side (see also Hilchot De'ot 4:5).
who couple. Who are joined together.
to insert like a brush into a tube. The insertion of the male organ into the female organ.
when they stand over the laundry. While they are washing clothes, and part of their body is exposed.
in the colored clothing of a woman he knows. Colored clothing, even when it is spread out and she is not wearing it, because when he sees it he remembers her and is aroused.
one who encounters a woman in the marketplace. A woman happens to be on his path and is walking in front of him.
runs and moves her aside. Goes around her so that she walks on his side or behind him.
this is among the lowliness of the ignorant. Base and contemptible conduct.
to put his hand on his genitals. To touch the testicles.
and even below his navel. From the navel downward.
he should not hold his organ. He should not hold the male organ.
who never looked at his circumcision. Who never gazed at his own nakedness.
for they take hold of the hearts of the holy. For the words of Torah draw the hearts of the holy sages, and not words of vanity.
close to their maturity. Close to their coming of age.
for if he leaves them they will come to harlotry or improper thoughts. That if he does not take trouble to marry them off, they may come to sin.
and it is forbidden to marry a woman to a minor; it is like harlotry. For a minor has no marriage, even by rabbinic law (Hilchot Ishut 3:19).
to remain without a wife. To remain unmarried.
and he should not marry a barren woman, an old woman, etc.. Because of the commandment to be fruitful and multiply (see Hilchot Ishut 15:7).
that she will never marry or will marry one who cannot father children or a eunuch. A man who cannot father children, since she is not commanded to be fruitful and multiply (ibid. 15:2).
for this leads to harlotry. For the couple are not suited to one another, and commit harlotry with others.
one who divorced his wife after marriage. That they already lived together and are accustomed to each other.
she may not live with him in a courtyard. In a house that shares a courtyard with his house.
in an alley. In the same street.
and a small village is treated as an alley. It is considered an alley for the purpose of this prohibition.
she appoints an agent to claim from him. And does not claim herself, so that there is no contact between them.
